articles.title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy benches rookie Cooper Pratt in 10-inning loss to Mets
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt certainly got the message sent by manager Pat Murphy on Tuesday night.  Murphy, the two-time defending National League...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Milwaukee Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt certainly got the message sent by manager Pat Murphy on Tuesday night.

Murphy, the two-time defending National League Manager of the Year, benched Pratt after he failed to get a bunt down and didn't run hard out of the batter's box on a bloop single during a 3-2 loss to the New York Mets in 10 innings.

"I've got to be better," Pratt said. "It's not winning baseball. I didn't help the team win and it won't happen again, that's for sure."

Batting ninth, Pratt was asked to bunt after Garrett Mitchell and Joey Ortiz opened the third with singles against Mets starter Zac Thornton. Pratt fouled off Thornton's first pitch and then pulled back his bat on the second one, a fastball right down the middle.

"We asked him to get a bunt down, pulled back on a strike, and that happens, maybe," Murphy said. "Trying to get a guy second and third for (Jackson) Chourio in a game where we weren't swinging it too good."

Swinging away with two strikes, Pratt fouled off the next two pitches before hitting a comebacker to Thornton, who fired to third to force Mitchell. Thornton then retired Chourio and Brice Turang to escape the jam.

Murphy was particularly annoyed in the fifth.

With one out, Pratt hit a flyball to shallow right field. He paused in the batter's box and gazed skyward for a moment before running at normal speed to first base.

The ball landed between three Mets in fair territory near the line and briefly bounced past right fielder Carson Benge. Pratt accelerated for a moment rounding first before heading back to the bag.

"No excuses. I should have been running hard, no matter if it is foul or fair," Pratt said. "I should have been (hustling) to get to second base."

Murphy immediately pulled Pratt for pinch-runner David Hamilton , who committed the walk-off throwing error at third base in the 10th.

Pratt, who turned 22 last week, made his major league debut on June 16 — about 2 1/2 months after the Brewers signed the shortstop prospect to an eight-year, $50.75 million contract.

"I love the kid and I believe in the kid immensely, but he's got to be a player that does those things," Murphy said. "It's just not tolerated. By anybody. It sends a message to everybody else, too — you've got to run."

Pratt looked surprised as he ran off the field. Television cameras caught him talking in the dugout to veteran teammate Sal Frelick.

"There's a certain way to play here and I may be new, but it doesn't matter," said Pratt, selected by Milwaukee in the sixth round of the 2023 amateur draft. "It's the way we're right through the organization from rookie ball to the big leagues. And I didn't do that. And I will do that. No excuses."

Pratt is batting .259 with two homers, 18 RBIs and 10 stolen bases in 49 games for the Brewers, who have the best record in the majors at 81-51 and are seeking a fourth straight NL Central crown.

"He's a great kid — it's not laziness," Murphy said. "You've got to have your head in the game. Because there's games like today, it comes down to (Francisco) Lindor's great catch or whatever it might be, an errant throw or whatever. You've got to be locked in if you're going to play at this level. So hopefully, a good learning experience."

Michigan State women's soccer is off to a hot and fast start to the 2026 season, and the recent rankings reflect that run.

After opening the season with a 2-0 win over Xavier, a team that received votes in the polls, the Spartans followed that up with a 1-0 win over Loyola Chicago, getting a quick 2-0 start at home. The biggest challenge of the young season came with a road trip to Chapel Hill, where the Spartans squared off with No. 6 North Carolina.

The Spartans defeated the Tar Heels, 3-2, earning a marquee win and a massive resume boost just a couple of weeks into the season.

Now, the latest United Coaches rankings came out and it has Michigan State ranked as the No. 3 team in the nation, trailing just Duke and Stanford.

The Spartans will be back in action this week with a pair of home games, hosting Eastern Michigan on Thursday before hosting No. 12 Colorado on Sunday.

articles.title: Raleigh continues homer barrage, Kirby fans 9 as Mariners beat Phillies 4-1
articles.summary: Cal Raleigh tied a team record with homers in four straight at-bats, George Kirby pitched one-run ball into the eighth inning and Seattle Mariners beat the P...
articles.body:
SEATTLE (AP) — Cal Raleigh tied a team record with homers in four straight at-bats, George Kirby pitched one-run ball into the eighth inning and Seattle Mariners beat the Philadelphia Phillies 4-1 on Tuesday night.

Raleigh led off the second inning against Philadelphia's Aaron Nola with a 362-foot shot to right field for his 18th homer of the season. It was his first time up after also homering in all three of his at-bats in a 9-2 win against the Phillies on Monday, matching the Seattle record of homers in four consecutive at-bats set by Mike Cameron on May 2, 2002.

Kirby (9-10) gave up one run on four hits and struck out nine in 7 2/3 innings. Jose Ferrer got the last out in the eighth and Andrés Muñoz pitched the ninth for his 24 save in 32 chances.

Nola (5-10) got the loss, allowing two runs on three hits with seven strikeouts over six innings.

Kirby was coming off a couple of tough outings, including giving up six first-inning runs in his last start against the Brewers . It looked as if he might be in trouble again when he allowed three straight singles in the second inning, including an RBI hit by Justin Crawford. Instead, Kirby got out of the jam and cruised the rest of the way.

The Mariners took a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning on Josh Naylor 's run-scoring single. Dominic Canzone added two more runs with a two-out, bases-loaded single to left-center off reliever Brooks Raley .

Raleigh became the first Seattle player to hit four home runs over two consecutive games since Kenji Johjima on June 24-27, 2006. Raleigh did walk in a plate appearance between homers on Monday, and walked his second time up on Tuesday before ending the streak with a sixth-inning strikeout.

Phillies LHP Jesús Luzardo (11-5, 3.35 ERA) takes on Mariners RHP Bryan Woo (9-8, 4.10) in the final of the three-game series Wednesday afternoon.

articles.title: LJ Phillips Jr. brings power running to Iowa
articles.summary: The Iowa running back room is filled with talented players. Lead rush Kamari Moulton is back, and the Hawkeyes added a coveted player out of the transfer por...
articles.body:
The Iowa running back room is filled with talented players. Lead rush Kamari Moulton is back, and the Hawkeyes added a coveted player out of the transfer portal.

LJ Phillips Jr. ran for nearly 2,000 yards last season at South Dakota. Now in Iowa City, he's enjoying being surrounded by other top running backs.

"I think I just bring a little bit of intensity, I just want to set the tone immediately. I think that's something that I've been working on is trying to set the tone immediately and I think that I can be that sparkplug maybe. There's competition everywhere you go, that's life," Phillips Jr. said. "Nothing in life is ever given to you or handed to you so that's just part of the job that comes with it. I think that this is a great place and I'm looking forward to competing with these guys. We have amazing running backs and to work with them is a blessing every day. It makes me better and they show me new things on how to be better and that's so special."

Iowa opens the year against Northern Illinois on Sept. 5.

articles.title: Bayern chiefs Eberl and Dreesen sign new contracts
articles.summary: Bayern Munich have extended the contracts of board member for sport Max Eberl and CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen.Both have signed new deals running until 2029, th...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich have extended the contracts of board member for sport Max Eberl and CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen.

Both have signed new deals running until 2029, the German champions confirmed on Tuesday evening.

"Continuity provides direction; stability brings strength: we need both to ensure FC Bayern continues to develop consistently at the very highest level," said chairman of the supervisory board Herbert Hainer.

"Especially in the dynamic competitive environment in which a top international club must forge its own path, consistency stands for a clear conviction. With Jan-Christian Dreesen, Max Eberl and Rouven Kasper, our board is ideally positioned to drive FC Bayern forward both in sporting and commercial terms and to maintain its leading position in Europe."

Dreesen joined Bayern as chief financial officer in 2013 before taking over as CEO 10 years later. He said:

"First of all, I would like to thank the supervisory board for their trust. I am delighted to be continuing my work at FC Bayern with energy and passion. As the executive board, together with our staff, members and fans, we intend to do everything in our power to ensure FC Bayern remains the top club of which we are all so proud. That is what drives us – and we still have a lot more to achieve."

Eberl, a former Bayern player who arrived from RB Leipzig to become board member for sport in March 2024, said:

"FC Bayern has been close to my heart ever since my time in the youth setup. So just like my fellow board members, I am committed to continuing along the path we have set out on and, in the interests of the entire FC Bayern family, to doing everything I can to ensure sporting success in the future. The supervisory board's confidence in me is a valued sign of support, which I am truly delighted about."

articles.title: Steelers Legend Ben Roethlisberger Breaks Silence on Browns Naming Deshaun Watson QB1
articles.summary: Former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger made his feelings clear on the Cleveland Browns naming Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback. The post Ste...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns made a predictable decision on Monday by naming Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback for the regular season. Watson competed with second-year player Shedeur Sanders , and all indications throughout training camp pointed toward Watson being the starter.

Watson hasn't played well since he was a member of the Houston Texans in 2020, and former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger made his feelings clear on Watson starting in Cleveland.

"Just like their playoff hopes. It's ended early before it even started," Roethlisberger said Tuesday on "FOOTBAHLIN With Ben Roethlisberger".

Roethlisberger knows all about bad quarterback play from the Browns. He spent 18 years with the Steelers and finished with a 26-2-1 regular-season record vs. Cleveland. But Watson might be the worst quarterback the Browns have had since Roethlisberger entered the NFL in 2004.

Even though Watson was the leader in the clubhouse all offseason, many people thought that was over after what he said about Cleveland fans.

Watson Went After Browns Fans After Losing to the Bills

The Browns fell to the Buffalo Bills in their second preseason game 31-7 on Saturday at Huntington Bank Field. But the biggest story of the game was the back-and-forth between the fans and Watson.

Watson entered the game in the third quarter, and Browns fans started to immediately boo. It also didn't help that Watson didn't play well, going 5 for 12, throwing for 36 yards and an interception.

The 30-year-old quarterback went to the podium after the game and criticized Browns fans for booing him.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said, via ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi. "It's a little bit [more] personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing. So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on."

Watson Took Back His Comments About Cleveland Fans

Watson did come out on Monday after the Browns named him the starter and apologized to the fans.

"I thought I was going to get a little different response," Watson added, "but I think my emotions got the best of me. My comments wasn't intending to go at any of the fans around in the city, because there's been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me. And I know the frustration. This organization has put a lot of investment in coming to get me back in '22, and things haven't been going the right direction that we thought it was. A lot of injuries, a lot of time off, and not putting the best football and my foot forward.

"I understand the frustration. I understand everything that kind of goes into that. And moving forward, I just want to focus on football, making sure that I'm putting the best product out there, having the best ability, because I thrive off the energy. I thrive off the energy of the fans. I thrive off the energy of the community. I thrive off all that stuff."

Many Browns fans don't seem willing to accept Watson as the starter, and it will be interesting to see how long he stays in that role. There is a good chance his last game as Cleveland's starter could be against the Steelers on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 4.

articles.title: Karateka
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Aún es pronto, porque el estreno ante el gran público se ha fijado para el 21 de septiembre en el marco del Festival de San Sebastián, porque a las salas llegará el 30 de octubre y porque ya nos encargaremos nosotros de recordárselo, pero sirvan estas líneas como primer apunte de que se viene gran película española de temática deportiva... Dirigida por Aritz Moreno, protagonizada por Andrea Ros y Patrick Criado, 'Karateka' recupera la historia de Sandra Sánchez, descartada por el sistema primero, la mejor de todos los tiempos después, y el increíble viaje que, de la mano de Jesús del Moral, entrenador y compañero de vida, emprendió para conquistar el oro olímpico a los 39 años en una categoría que contempla habitualmente la retirada casi una década antes. Los que hemos tenido la suerte de asistir a un pase previo dejamos constancia aquí de que el largometraje merece la pena sin necesidad de que el espectador sea especialista en (o aficionado) al karate, por actuaciones, por ritmo, por fotografía, por banda sonora, por tantas otras cosas, pero es que, además, los que siguieron durante años ese periplo de Sandra y Jesús (nadie mejor que mis compañeros Almudena Rivera y Andrés García) dan fe de que resulta absolutamente fiel a la realidad incluso cuando se acerca a los aspectos más dolorosos de la misma. Y resulta curioso también que Sandra doble a la actriz que hace de Sandra en una película sobre Sandra, pero es que la talaverana y su pareja participaron activamente como asesores durante todo el proceso creativo, ayudando a que se trasladen a la pantalla no solo la práctica deportiva, sino también los valores y la filosofía que definen el karate. Andrea y Patrick, sometidos a un severo cambio de hábitos y a un régimen de duros entrenamientos, admiten ahora que esta película les ha cambiado la vida. Pues eso: que apetecía contarlo pero que tiempo habrá. Y mientras, 'smile and relax' (cuando la vean entenderán esto último...)

articles.title: Penguins’ Bill Zonnon Dark Horse Candidate to make Opening Night Roster
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins are a team that is trying to get younger and one of their most recent first-round draft picks fits that description in Bill Zonnon. F...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Penguins are trying to get younger on their NHL roster. They proved that more recently last season when Ben Kindel and Harrison Brunicke made the opening night roster. But they have another player in Bill Zonnon looking to make this season's opening night roster.

Zonnon was in the same draft class and the same round (first round in 2025) as Kindel was. Zonnon was the Penguins second first-round selection in 2025 behind Kindel and then came Will Horcoff.

Zonnon actually got into a few playoff games for the Wilkes-Barre Scranton Penguins this past season and looked ready. But it is all about showing up and showing out at this year's NHL training camp and impressing Dan Muse and Kyle Dubas enough. The kid has the talent.

Bill Zonnon fits the timeline of what the Penguins want in their roster

It is no secret that the Penguins along with Dubas and Muse want to make the team younger, faster, and hard to play against. Zonnon fits that bill as he was a first-round pick in 2025 and is quite fast and uses his size to frustrate opponents.

Zonnon should have plenty of opportunities to find his game and impress the staff in camp coming up soon and in any preseason games he gets into. His experience in Wilkes-Barre being able to play playoff games and score a few goals, is huge for his chances for this year's NHL roster.

Bill Zonnon is a guy that was really valued in the 2025 draft class and Dubas took a swing on him. It is not yet known if the pick has paid off as the kid has not been able to debut with the Penguins yet.

It says a lot that Zonnon was able to go from his junior team to Wilkes-Barre on the fourth line to even in the top six in a span of a few games. It is clear that especially in the AHL that he is trusted enough to go from the bottom six to the top six in a hurry.

Penguins fans should be excited to see Bill Zonnon and what he can do in training camp and the preseason coming up. It is not necessarily a lock for the kid to make the opening night roster, but he has a chance.

Even if Zonnon does not make the opening night roster, he would start the year in Wilkes-Barre and that would not be bad for his development. He would certainly get a call to Pittsburgh at some point in the season to get a crack with the veterans.

articles.title: A’s Even Series with 4-2 Victory
articles.summary: Gage Jump Shines Again
articles.body:
The Athletics faced the Minnesota Twins seeking to even the series ahead of Wednesday's finale. That is exactly what the A's did, prevailing 4-2 thanks to a quality start from Gage Jump, contributions from outfielders Carlos Cortes and Lawrence Butler and a bullpen that held a late lead— something A's relievers have struggled to do lately.

With two outs in the second inning, A's shortstop Alika Williams doubled for his team's first hit against Twins starter Taj Bradley . Left fielder Carlos Cortes did not let that scoring opportunity go to waste. He hit his eighth home run of the season, a two-run shot onto the berm in right field, putting the Athletics ahead 2-0.

Athletics starter Gage Jump turned in a scoreless first three innings, preventing the Twins from scoring early for a second straight game. The top of the third was especially critical, as his team had just taken the lead in the previous inning.

Jump Unfazed by A's Little League Defense

The Athletics' defense betrayed them with two outs in the fourth. Twins first baseman Royce Lewis ' infield pop-up was ruled a single, yet it arguably should have been ruled an error after none of the A's infielders could make the catch. Lewis then stole second on a pickoff throw that A's first baseman Tommy White failed to catch. Jump fortunately escaped that jam by striking out the next batter he faced.

Jump continued rolling, racking up nine strikeouts over six scoreless innings while keeping his team's two-run lead intact. Meanwhile, Bradley rebounded from Cortes' home run to throw three straight scoreless innings, preventing the hosts from extending their lead in this pitching duel between two high-octane arms. In the bottom of the fifth, Bradley turned in the first immaculate inning in Twins history.

With two outs in the sixth inning, A's right fielder Lawrence Butler recorded his second single of the night. Butler then raced around to narrowly slide in safely on White's RBI double off the center field wall. A's second baseman Donovan Walton made it three consecutive two-out hits as his RBI single brought White home to put the Green and Gold up 4-0.

Jump's shutout bid ended in the seventh inning when Kaelen Culpepper's RBI double made it a 4-1 game. That was the last batter Jump faced. The A's rookie southpaw allowed two runs on three hits over 6 1/3 innings, walking two and striking out nine.

Left-hander Hogan Harris replaced Jump. After Brooks Lee doubled on a bloop hit that fell out of Walton's glove, Victor Caratini 's RBI groundout cut the A's lead to two runs. Gelof made a nice play on that grounder, preventing a second run from scoring. That loomed large, as Harris wiggled out of the jam, stranding two runners.

With two outs in the bottom of the seventh, Athletics center fielder Henry Bolte hit his first major league triple. That hit not only knocked Bradley out of the game but also forced Twins center fielder Byron Buxton to leave with an injury. The A's could not come through with a two-out RBI hit for a second consecutive inning, as Minnesota reliever AJ Minter struck out Jeff McNeil to end the seventh.

After A's right-hander Luis Medina retired the side in the eighth, Elvis Alvarado entered for the save opportunity in the top of the ninth. Alvarado said good night to the Twins, securing his fourth save, Jump's sixth win and ,most importantly, giving the A's a chance to win the series tomorrow evening.

The Athletics will send right-hander J.T. Ginn to the mound for the rubber match, while Minnesota will counter with left-hander Connor Prielipp.

articles.title: Ryan Waldschmidt hits game-winning 2-run HR with 2 outs in 9th to send D-backs past Cubs 5-4
articles.summary: Pinch-hitter Ryan Waldschmidt hit a game-winning, two-run homer with two outs in the ninth inning and the Arizona Diamondbacks rallied to stun the Chicago Cu...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Pinch-hitter Ryan Waldschmidt hit a game-winning, two-run homer with two outs in the ninth inning and the Arizona Diamondbacks rallied to stun the Chicago Cubs 5-4 on Tuesday night.

The D-backs pulled one game behind the San Diego Padres for the final NL wild-card spot.

Trailing 4-3 in the ninth, Tim Tawa coaxed a one-out walk from Jacob Webb to start the decisive rally. Ildemaro Vargas flew out to right field for the second out before pinch-runner Jose Fernandez stole second base. Waldschmidt — a rookie — then launched a no-doubt homer over the left field fence to set off a raucous celebration.

It was Waldschmidt's second walk-off homer of the season.

Arizona trailed 4-0 in the eighth before mounting a two-out rally against reliever Daniel Palencia . Gabriel Moreno hit a check swing RBI double that hugged the first base line and stayed fair before Geraldo Perdomo 's two-run single cut the deficit to 4-3. Webb relieved Palencia and coaxed a ground out from Max Kepler to end the threat.

Ian Happ hit a three-run homer in the fourth to push the Cubs ahead 3-0. Michael Busch 's RBI single in the sixth made it 4-0. Busch and Seiya Suzuki both had two hits.

The D-backs' rally ruined a great outing for Clay Holmes , who breezed through the D-backs' lineup, giving up two singles and two walks while striking out five over seven scoreless innings. The right-hander has given up just one earned run over his past 19 innings, spanning three starts.

Arizona's Brandon Pfaadt (7-2) gave up four runs on six hits and two walks, striking out three. He didn't allow a hit over the first three innings, but gave up a single and a double in the fourth before Happ's three-run homer.

The D-backs send LHP Eduardo Rodriguez (13-4, 2.61 ERA) to the mound to face Cubs LHP Matthew Boyd (8-2, 4.15).

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes Sued by Former WR in Unusual Transfer Portal Twist
articles.summary: The Hurricanes face a lawsuit from former receiver Cam Vaughn with an unusually familiar transfer portal argument at its center. The post Miami Hurricanes Su...
articles.body:
The Miami Hurricanes have made the transfer portal one of the foundations of their roster-building under Mario Cristobal. Now, a former Miami wide receiver is taking the program to court over what he says is the school's refusal to let him use it.

Cam Vaughn filed a lawsuit against Miami and the NCAA on Aug. 25 seeking the ability to enter the transfer portal after the Hurricanes dismissed him from the football program on Aug. 17. Vaughn transferred to Miami from West Virginia in January.

Considering Miami's recent history with cornerback Xavier Lucas and quarterback Darian Mensah, Vaughn's dispute with the university makes this an intriguing development.

Cam Vaughn Lawsuit Targets Miami, NCAA Over Portal Access

On3's Alex Byington, citing reporting from Pete Nakos, reported that Vaughn's representatives filed the lawsuit in Miami-Dade County against the university and NCAA.

Vaughn's representative, Blake Sercye, said Miami canceled the receiver's scholarship and then declined to make the waiver request needed for him to enter the portal outside the normal transfer window.

"On August 17, 2026, Miami dismissed Cam and cancelled his scholarship with no written explanation, no identified rule violation, and no hearing. Miami then refused to submit the waiver request the NCAA requires so that he can enter the transfer portal — leaving Cam without the ability to pursue his education or a team to play for. We are asking the court to hold Miami and the NCAA responsible for their failures to Cam, and grant him the relief he needs so that he can continue his education and career," Sercye said.

Those are allegations made by Vaughn's representative. On3's report did not include a response from Miami.

Vaughn has logged 83 passes for 1,344 yards and nine touchdowns between Jacksonville State and West Virginia in the last three years.

Miami Benefited From Similar Portal Fights With Xavier Lucas, Darian Mensah

Miami's recruitment of Lucas and Mensah previously makes this entire situation a bit awkward.

A year before Vaughn's lawsuit, defensive back Xavier Lucas wanted to leave Wisconsin. The Miami Herald's Jordan McPherson reported the Badgers did not enter his name into the transfer portal after he submitted his paperwork, citing a two-year NIL agreement they maintained was binding.

Lucas publicly accused Wisconsin of impeding his ability to transfer. He eventually unenrolled from Wisconsin and enrolled at Miami in January 2025 without ever appearing in the portal.

Wisconsin later sued Miami in June 2025, alleging the Hurricanes had impermissibly contacted Lucas and induced him to break his agreement. Miami denied wrongdoing and moved to dismiss the lawsuit.

Miami found itself in another transfer fight in January 2026. The Miami Herald's Barry Jackson and Jordan McPherson reported Duke and quarterback Darian Mensah reached a settlement after the Blue Devils sued to keep him from leaving, arguing his multiyear NIL agreement remained enforceable. The settlement cleared Mensah to transfer , and he committed to Miami later that day.

The circumstances aren't identical. Wisconsin's fight with Lucas and Duke's with Mensah centered heavily on contractual obligations, while Vaughn's representatives are challenging what happened after Miami dismissed him and canceled his scholarship.

Still, the common thread is difficult to miss.

Twice in a little more than a year, Miami benefited when prominent players sought to leave schools that tried to restrict their movement. According to Vaughn's lawsuit, the Hurricanes are now refusing to take the administrative step he needs to pursue the same freedom elsewhere.

Whether Vaughn's legal claims succeed is for the court to decide. For a program that has been one of college football's most aggressive portal shoppers, simply being on this side of the dispute creates an unusually uncomfortable look.

articles.title: Kirb’ed: Mariners 4, Phillies 1
articles.summary: Stifled in Seattle
articles.body:
The offense continued to sputter to begin the road trip and wasted another encouraging effort from Aaron Nola as the Philadelphia Phillies (73-60) dropped their second straight against the Seattle Mariners (64-69) on Tuesday night.

Mariners' starter, George Kirby , kept the offense in check most of the night but allowed the first run of the game in the second inning as Bryson Stott , Brandon Marsh and Justin Crawford strung together a trio of one-out singles.

After registering his first three-homer game last night, Cal Raleigh tied the game with a solo shot to begin the bottom of the second for his fourth home run in as many at bats.

Nola conceded the tie in the bottom of the sixth on an RBI single by Josh Naylor following a one-out single and a steal by Julio Rodriguez .

Aside from the two runs on three hits and three walks, Nola looked to still be in command of his stuff entering the seventh inning with 92 pitches. Don Mattingly opted to give way to Orion Kerkering who, after getting a ground out to start the inning, loaded the bases on a hit by pitch, single and a walk. Kerkering induced a pop out by Randy Arozarena for the second out and Mattingly went to Brooks Raley to face the lefty, Dominic Canzone . Raley left a 1-1 sweeper over the plate that Canzone laced to left for a two-RBI single to effectively put the game away.

In Kerkering and Raley's defense, the offense had no answers for Kirby & Co. Kirby begrudging left the game two outs into the eighth after allowing a hit to Bryce Harper but the minor threat was quickly erased by Jose Ferrer on a Luis Arraez ground out.

Jonathan Bowlan pitched a scoreless bottom of the eighth and Alec Bohm and Crawford worked a pair of walks against Mariners' closer, Andres Munoz, to create a two-out threat in the ninth, but a pinch-hitting-for-Garrett-Stubbs Bryan De La Cruz struck out on four pitches to close it out.

The Phillies will try to stave off the sweep tomorrow afternoon as Jesus Luzardo faces off against Bryan Woo .

articles.title: ‘That’s Your Job to Hate Them’ — Urban Meyer Issues No-Nonsense Take on Kyle Whittingham, Bryce Underwood Downplaying Ohio State Rivalry
articles.summary: Former coach Urban Meyer understands Kyle Whittingham’s point. He just thinks Michigan’s new head coach is approaching the Ohio State rivalry with a little t...
articles.body:
Former coach Urban Meyer understands Kyle Whittingham's point. He just thinks Michigan's new head coach is approaching the Ohio State rivalry with a little too much common sense.

After Whittingham rejected the idea that he needs to personally hate Ryan Day and Bryce Underwood called Ohio State "just another game," Meyer offered a very different philosophy. For the former Buckeyes coach, hatred does not have to be personal to be useful.

Urban Meyer Says Hatred Has a Place in The Game

During a recent The Triple Option podcast episode, Meyer said he never personally hated Jim Harbaugh or Brady Hoke, but that distinction disappeared once Michigan became the opponent.

"Do I hate them? Absolutely, I hate them, and that's your job to hate them," Meyer said. "You got to play the game."

Meyer predicted Whittingham may develop more of that edge after his first trip to Columbus as Michigan's head coach. More importantly, he argued that a coach at either program has to understand what the rivalry means to the people around it.

"You're not going to change that," Meyer said. "So play the game."

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Meyer then took the argument beyond rivalry theater. He said love, fear, and hate were the three greatest motivators he used when preparing his teams, and he deliberately tried to create situations that made his players angry before games.

"I wanted my team so angry coming out of that tunnel that they played with nastiness and violence to them," Meyer said.

There is some history behind the conviction. Meyer went 7-0 against Michigan during his seven seasons at Ohio State, never experiencing the rivalry from the losing locker room.

Bryce Underwood Adds Another Layer to Michigan's Approach

Whittingham's comments drew attention after he said a rivalry can be intense without a "hatred factor" and questioned whether hating Ohio State would improve Michigan's chances of winning.

Underwood then told NBC Sports' John Fanta in an original interview that the Buckeyes are "just another game, just guys in a different color."

Underwood will have a chance to test that approach again after a difficult first appearance in The Game. Ohio State beat Michigan 27-9 last November, with Underwood completing eight of 18 passes for 63 yards and an interception.

His freshman season still showed plenty of upside. Underwood finished with a 78.0 PFSN QB Impact grade, ranking No. 79 nationally, while throwing for 2,428 yards and adding 392 rushing yards.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free College Fantasy Simulator

Michigan travels to Columbus on Nov. 28 for the 122nd meeting between the programs. Whittingham has made clear that he desperately wants to win it, even if he does not embrace the language surrounding it.

Meyer's message is simpler. In this rivalry, hatred is not supposed to describe the person across the field. It is supposed to help beat the colors they are wearing.

articles.title: 5 players to watch for Commanders in joint practice vs. Ravens
articles.summary: We look at five players to watch in Wednesday's joint practice with the Ravens.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have less than a week to trim their roster from 90 to 53 players. The Commanders made one tough decision on Tuesday, releasing former starting safety Will Harris . Once it became clear that Washington wasn't keeping Harris, the team wanted to do right by him and give him a head start on finding a new team before hundreds of players hit free agency at the same time on Sunday.

With Harris off the bubble and no longer on the roster, which Washington players need to shine during Wednesday's joint practice with the Ravens , followed by Friday's preseason finale?

Here are five players to watch in Wednesday's joint practice with Baltimore :

With Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Jeremy McNichols battling injuries and Jerome Ford already gone, Henry has another chance to shine. After an impressive preseason opener against the Dolphins , Henry crashed back down to earth last week. As of now, Henry probably hasn't done quite enough to earn a spot on the 53. He must make it hard for the Commanders to cut him. He'll likely split time with Rachaad White and fellow rookie Kaytron Allen . Henry needs to make the most out of every touch.

Last week, head coach Dan Quinn said he wanted to see the rookie sixth-round pick get more work at guard after an impressive first performance. Quinn said that because whoever makes the roster as a backup offensive lineman must be able to play multiple spots. However, after seeing Julian Good-Jones' struggles last week in place of Nick Allegretti , Gulbin should handle every rep, regardless of who is playing quarterback. Gulbin got more work with starter Jayden Daniels during Tuesday's practice, and that should be the case on Wednesday.

Williams performed well against the Lions . His catch across the middle showed his potential. He has great hands, runs terrific routes, and gets an excellent release off the line of scrimmage. We'd like to see Williams work with Washington's starters, which means being on the field with Terry McLaurin , Stefon Diggs , and Daniels, and facing Baltimore's first-team defense. This will be a great evaluation tool for Williams.

Johnny Newton's injury created an opening for Ricky Barber Jr. While many believe veteran Shy Tuttle could win the last defensive tackle spot, Barber is having a strong camp. The second-year former UDFA has flashed in each game. He needs more reps against starters to gauge his progress. The joint practice would allow defensive coordinator Daronte Jones to see Barber against stiffer competition.

We've mostly stuck with the theme of younger players. However, due to Washington's concerns at cornerback, Moreau stands a good chance of making the Commanders' roster. With Trey Amos still sidelined, Washington's top four corners are Mike Sainristil , Amik Robertson , Rasul Douglas and Moreau. The Amos injury almost assures that the Commanders will keep five cornerbacks. Moreau has played a lot of football, including for Jones, but the Commanders need to test him against another team.

articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are waiting on pins and needles for the possible return of the retired defensive star, Aaron Donald, who announced his retirement on soc...
articles.body:
Is the football world still waiting for Aaron Donald to decide whether he'll return from retirement for 2026, while another Donald-Rams workout has taken place at the Woodland Hills facility?

Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-USA TODAY Sports

Aug 27, 2016; Denver , CO, USA; Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) during the second half of a preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Sports Authority Field at Mile High. The Broncos defeated the Rams 17-9.

The Los Angeles Rams are waiting on pins and needles for the possible return of the retired defensive star, who announced his retirement on social media in March 2024.

Talk of a comeback first gained traction after Donald admitted that the Rams' blockbuster trade for Myles Garrett got him thinking about whether that fire can light back up.

On Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay gets honest about the team's plans and explained that the front office has plans for the alternative outcome.

"If he ends up doing it later, you could hypothetically–but that's not even part of our thought process," McVay told reporters . "Our thought process has been let's look at a 53 with him and a 53 not including him, and what does that look like?"

Donald worked out with the Rams for the second time on Aug. 16, and continues to put in work as he weighs a return to the NFL.

Dwight Freeney demands the real Aaron Donald

Former NFL edge Dwight Freeney says there's a difference between decent shape and football shape.

"If Aaron is Aaron… oh, it's gonna be a problem… It gotta be Aaron Donald as we remember, not just a guy with Aaron Donald's name."

Stafford, who played with and won a Super Bowl alongside Donald, said that the guy's an absolute monster in the weight room. The quarterback has so much respect for him.

"Whatever's right for Aaron is right for us," he said . "And if that's, 'Hey, I don't think I can do it,' Hey man, I appreciate it. Thanks for everything you always did, and then, giving it a rip and trying to see if you could do it again."

Rams roster decisions are looming as the regular-season opener against the San Francisco 49ers draws closer.

Whether the 35-year-old stays put or suits up, Donald is considered one of the greatest defensive players of all time.

articles.title: Wojo: Tigers flash glimpses of future as playoff light fades
articles.summary: The Tigers aren’t looking ahead to the future, at least not officially, but on nights like this, there are glimpses of the big-picture goal.
articles.body:
Detroit — The Tigers aren't looking ahead to the future, at least not officially. The playoffs are almost out of sight, if not quite out of mind.

But on nights like this, there are glimpses, micro-views of the big-picture goal. The Tigers have played 11 rookies this season, and four of them were key in a much-needed 4-1 victory over Tampa Bay Tuesday night at Comerica Park. The starting pitcher, Jackson Jobe , is 24 but not a rookie. In only his fourth start in 14 months after Tommy John surgery, he expanded his arsenal, maintained his composure and took a step forward.

That's what it's about now for the Tigers (62-70), who snapped a six-game losing streak that just about squashed their faint playoff hopes. The A.L. remains muddled with mediocrity, so the Tigers are only four games out of the wild card, but trail six teams. Because they've defied ridiculous odds before, we're legally required to note their chances currently stand at 3.8%.

Yes, that's better than the 0.2% odds they overcame in 2024. But the chances of overcoming astronomical odds twice in three years have to be more astronomical. With 30 games left, there's no sense belaboring the obvious, not when the future is up now. We'll have ample opportunity to pick through all that was squandered, and the nasty mistakes that were made.

In the meantime, the Tigers' young talent is gathering expedited experience. There was rookie reliever Drew Sommers throwing 1.2 shutout innings to earn his first MLB victory and lower his ERA to 2.93. There was rookie Hao-Yu Lee lacing a two-out RBI single in the seventh to expand the lead to 4-1. There was Kevin McGonigle, playing flawless defense at third and short, the favorite to win A.L. Rookie of the Year.

And there was rookie centerfielder Max Clark slamming his second career home run — his first in Comerica Park — and racing around the bases so quickly, he almost ran up the back of runner Javy Báez.

"I completely blacked out, it was a really cool moment," Clark said. "I looked up and I could see (Báez's) number within touching distance. I started to panic and slowed down a little bit."

Clark, 21, runs as if trying make up for lost time, or trying to catch his best friend, McGonigle. Clark, the No. 3 overall pick in 2023, is hitting .247 with a .704 OPS, and already looks like a speedy mainstay in center field. He prides himself on his defense to the point he sounded fairly disgusted after he overran a hit by Liam Hicks in the fourth inning, leading to the Rays ' only run. Hicks was awarded a double, but even Clark knew it was an error.

"It took a weird hop, but it's unacceptable regardless," Clark said. "It's almost embarrassing to be completely honest."

Clark is honest and glib, a spark plug in every way. AJ Hinch loved that Clark was so annoyed by his misplay he turned into Mad Max.

"It fired me up that he's pissed," Hinch said. "He needs to make that play, and he's not gonna give himself any grace. That's the high standard we need. He plays a very fast center field. He's going to be really good because of that. He goes home with a learning lesson, and makes my job a little easier."

Lots of lessons are being learned by the Tigers, young and old. In the offseason, they'll need to show they grasped something. It starts with president of baseball operations Scott Harris, who will have to explain his signings and acquisitions — and lack thereof — and how the Tigers' offense and bullpen became so maddeningly inconsistent. The Tigers have ridden one of the craziest rollercoasters in memory, rising from 16 games under .500 to within a whiff of first place, and then down again. The latest rough stretch coincided with the loss of Riley Greene to a hamstring injury, with the Tigers 3-10 in his absence.

None of the rookies this season were around for the 2024 miracle, so they're just trying to navigate the daily grind. And even as the Tigers fall out of the playoff picture, there's valuable experience to be gained.

Jobe was so annoyed by his "godawful" change-up in his last rocky outing against the White Sox , he worked on ramping up his curveball velocity. He's healthy but still shaking off rust, and threw 86 pitches in 4.1 innings. He battled a potent lineup and a Rays team with the best record in the A.L., striking out four, walking three and escaping a base-loaded jam in the fourth when Tampa Bay took a 1-0 lead.

"I'm just figuring out what works, trying different things, making some changes when I can," said Jobe, the third overall pick in 2021. "Today the curveball was very big for me, something I've been struggling with. It kind of turned into a real weapon, in my opinion. It definitely felt like a momentum shifter, potentially. We still have a lot of good energy in this clubhouse, hopefully we can turn it around."

Potentially and hopefully are the salient words for the Tigers now. Potential is what the Tigers are hoping to cash in, if not now, soon. You see glimpses of the confidence that made Jobe such a touted prospect, along with his fastball that touches 100. You see a star in McGonigle. You also see holes on a roster that will require some veteran help.

We'll see one wayward piece of their past this weekend when Tarik Skubal comes to town with the Dodgers . Has that trade cost the Tigers in the short term? Of course. But when Hinch hears his young guys beating themselves up for miscues, vowing to get better, his mood brightens, ever so slightly.

"You gotta let them grow up," Hinch said. "Sometimes, at this level, at this time of year, and where our team is, it's hard to recognize that."

It's not hard to recognize the potential of the Tigers' young players. It's also not hard to recognize the current odds, and the reality of a season in which way too many opportunities were wasted.

articles.title: Brevard HEAT's dynamic offense leads to sweep of Melbourne CC
articles.summary: After both teams won all their first-week matches, Brevard HEAT showed its potential with a sweep of Melbourne Central Catholic to go to 4-0.
articles.body:
Melbourne Central Catholic traveled to Palm Bay on Aug. 25 to play Brevard HEAT in a matchup featuring undefeated teams.

Brevard HEAT's strong serving and balanced attack propelled the Firehawks to the sweep 25-12, 25-18, 25-16.

"Our first set was really strong," Brevard HEAT head coach Darrah Bowen said. "We struggled a little bit set two and three and just played.

The Firehawks ended the match with 26 kills and 14 aces. Senior Aine Hanley led the attack with 6 kills and 3 aces. Senior setter Anna Livengood comprised nearly have of the service aces with 6 to go with 2 kills. Sophomore Charis Bennett and senior Brooke Arce recorded 6 and 5 kills, respectively.

"We really work hard to make our serve an offensive weapon instead of just getting it over and it showed," Bowen said.

Firehawks take down Hustlers in girls volleyball

Livengood's presence was felt all over the court. The senior setter recorded a pair of dump kills in the first set. In set two, Livengood served 3 aces in 4 points fueling an 11-4 run to close out the second set.

"Just my coach, my teammates staying behind me after I missed my first serve," Livengood said. "My coach and my teammates said serve it this time. We're here to back you up. Them pushing me instead of being angry with me led me to get those aces."

Livengood, who dished out 52 assists through the first three games, is still building chemistry with the new players on the floor following graduations and transfers. She led the team with 680 assists last season.

"Coming into this season, we have a lot of key pieces missing. We have a couple girls that went and played college so just missing them this year," Livengood said. "We've had a couple girls come in transferring. A lot of new pieces we weren't really expecting that really came in and helped make this team what it is now."

Bowen coaches Hanley during the club season. The senior, who recorded 128 kills last season, has embraced playing back row this season and has become a productive defender with 40 digs through the first three games.

"(Hanley) came into the (club) team where she had to learn to be a leader. She embraced it and became the strongest player we had. This year, she just rolled with that," Bowen said. "She wasn't quite sure coming in what she looked like as an outside because she set for us the last couple years. She has just owned that back row, she talks loud, she encourages everyone. I don't want to take her off the court."

Brevard HEAT improved to 4-0 with its third-straight sweep after defeating Space Coast in 4 sets in the opener.

"I think we got a pretty solid group," Livengood said. "I think we're going to go pretty far in districts, regionals. I think as long as we come and reach our potential, I think we could go pretty far."

The Firehawks head to Merritt Island Christian on Aug. 27 before a regional final rematch with St. Edward's on Aug. 28. Bowen said she believes the team is well positioned to reach the state semifinals for the second time in 3 years.

"We've got a little more depth just from our front row and our back row where we didn't have that last year," Bowen said. "When we were missing a player, we were stuck. This year we actually have some height and it's going to make a difference."

Errors plagued Melbourne Central Catholic in its first defeat of the season. The Hustlers ended the game with 32 attacking and service errors to go with 14 kills and 5 aces.

"It wasn't our best. I just think we underestimated our competition after winning a few games in a row," Melbourne Central Catholic head coach Jessica McGuire said. "When the atmosphere is different, ceiling's lower and the court is shorter, it's easier to get rattled. We had our good moments, but we need to be more consistent."

MCC senior Catalina Mendoza led the team with 6 kills and 2 aces. Junior Rossi Deane chipped in with 5 kills.

In the back row, senior Emma Martin has anchored Hustlers defense. Martin dug a team-high 27 balls raising her total to 66 through four matches.

"(Martin's) been great," McGuire said. "Lots of awesome digs and usually amazing passes as well. She's really great and talkative and a good senior leader on our team."

In McGuire's first season, MCC began the season 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Hustlers swept Cocoa Beach and defeated Titusville in five sets. The fast start, McGuire said, injected confidence into the squad.

"That was awesome. It was tough and that set the tone. We had our best setter get injured. She tore her ACL and we were able to pull off that game," McGuire said. "We beat Cocoa Beach and Titusville and they were all crying at the end. They hadn't beaten them additionally with a whole new lineup."

Melbourne Central Catholic hosts West Shore on Aug. 26 and Edgewood on Aug. 27. In search for its first winning season since 2014, McGuire said she believes the team is capable of turning heads this season.

"We are trying to win at least 75% of our games," McGuire said. "I think they only won 30% last year and I hope it's higher and we're ending up first or second in our district tournament and to go far. I think they have the capability. They just have to believe it because they've come from like 12 years of losing seasons."

Odyssey Charter def. Halifax Academy 3-0 (25-16, 25-12, 25-11)

Odyssey Charter swept Halifax Academy in its season opener behind 27 kills and 23 aces. Senior Lily Gilmore recorded 6 kills and a team-high 6 aces. Freshman Karigan Ford-Torres spiked a team-high 8 kills to go with 5 aces. Senior Lauren Janesky tallied 20 assists and 5 aces.

The Titans begin the year 1-0 and they'll head to Pineapple Cove Palm Bay on Aug. 27.

Edgewood def. Rockledge 3-0 (25-18, 25-19, 25-13)

The Red Wolves picked up their second sweep of the season as sophomore Maya Ferguson led the attack with 9 kills and 7 aces. They finished with 26 kills and 18 aces as a team.

Junior Adison Carter posted a double-double of 15 assists and 10 digs. Junior Kelsey Kennedy and senior Macy Ferguson spiked 7 and 5 kills, respectively.

Edgewood improved to 3-1 and it'll play back-to-back road games at Space Coast on Aug. 26 and Melbourne Central Catholic on Aug. 27. Rockledge fell to 0-4 and it'll host Eau Gallie on Sept. 1.

Viera def. Holy Trinity 3-0 (28-26, 27-25. 25-20)

In a hotly contested match, Viera picks up its second home win in a row with a sweep of Holy Trinity.

The Hawks moved to 3-0 and will head to Astronaut on Aug. 27. The Tigers lost their second game in a row and will bring a 1-2 record into their next match versus Vero Beach on Aug. 26 before heading to Orangewood Christian on Aug. 27.

Merritt Island def. New Smyrna Beach 3-0 (25-21, 25-19, 25-10)

The Mustangs finished with three attackers in double-figure kills. Junior Ema Michell recorded a dozen kills with junior Lydia Scott and senior Bella Becker finishing with 11 kills each.

Michell and senior Amber Ives served 4 aces. Scott blocked 4 shots with Michell, Becker and junior Peyton Riordan ending the match with 3 blocks each. Ives completed the night with 19 assists.

Merritt Island heads into a big weekend with a 4-0 record. The Mustangs play back-to-back road games against state finalists in defending Class 3A champion Calvary Christian Clearwater on Aug. 28 and Class 2A runner-up First Baptist Academy on Aug. 29.

Bayside def. Cocoa 3-0 (25-16, 25-11, 25-2)

Bayside entered the win column for the first time this season sweeping Cocoa at home.

The Bears improve to 1-2 and they'll play at Cocoa Beach on Aug. 27. The Tigers drop to 0-2 and will host the Minutemen on Aug. 26 before heading to Palm Bay on Aug. 27.

Melbourne def. Cocoa Beach 3-0 (25-19, 25-8, 25-13)

Melbourne earned the sweep in its home opener. The Bulldogs went 3-2 in the SSAA Invitational on Aug. 21-22 earning wins over Geneva Classical Academy, Evangelical Christian and Cambridge Christian. Melbourne lost to Lakewood Ranch and Southland Christian.

The Bulldogs moved to 5-3 and they'll play at Heritage on Aug. 27.

Satellite def. Titusville 3-0 (25-11, 25-19, 25-18)

The Scorpions won their third straight match in a game featuring state playoff teams from a year ago.

Titusville senior Hayden Thibert led the team with 10 kills. Sophomore Natalie Regan recorded 8 kills and a team-high 6 aces. Seniors Zoe Silva and Paisley Perry recorded double-figures assists with 14 and 12, respectively.

Satellite takes a 3-1 record into its next match at Merritt Island on Sept. 1. Titusville brings a 1-3 record into its next match versus Space Coast on Aug. 27.

Space Coast def. Eau Gallie 3-0 (25-5, 25-13, 25-13)

The Vipers spoil the season and home opener for Eau Gallie with a convincing sweep. They improve to 3-1 and they'll face Edgewood on Aug. 26 and Titusville on Aug. 27.

Eau Gallie starts the season 0-1 and it'll head to West Shore on Aug. 27.

articles.title: Holy Waldschmidt! Dbacks 5, Cubs 4
articles.summary: Mark Grace perhaps said it best in the postgame show when he said, “Im not sure we have seen a more unlikely Dbacks win the season” The almost Dback Clay Hol...
articles.body:
Mark Grace perhaps said it best in the postgame show when he said, "Im not sure we have seen a more unlikely Dbacks win the season"

The almost Dback Clay Holmes shut this Dbacks offense down for 7 innings. The Dbacks had a deal in place for Holmes per multiple reports but the deal fell through at the last minute due to medicals. The fact that he was almost a Dback made the first 7 innings of this game sting all that much more, especially given the current status of this rotation.

Brandon Pfaadt was pretty good today pitching into the 7 th inning tonight and allowing 4 runs while keeping his team within striking distance. The Cubs have the 2 nd best offense in the league and Pfaadt did a decent enough job of keeping them in check. His first 3 innings were pretty easy getting lots of soft contact, however he gave up a 3 run HR in the 4 th inning on a hanging curveball to Ian Happ . Most importantly however, like I mentioned earlier, he was able to settle back in after the home run and give his team 6.2 innings against a red hot offense.

The Dbacks offense finally woke up in the 8 th inning as they were able to finally get on the board with 3 runs due to some linked up at bats with a couple of walks and a huge double from the red hot Gabi Moreno and a single from Geraldo Perdomo . When this offense has been clicking this season, it seems as though it is starting with the bottom of the order getting on base for the top of the order.

The story of the game however was Ryan Waldsschmidt who for the second time this season hit a walkoff home run off of a contending team's closer. This time it came as a pinch hitter with 2 outs in the bottom of the 9 th with Jose Fernandez pinch running at first base for Tim Tawa . The Dbacks were inches away from losing this game as Jose Fernandez was narrowly able to steal 2 nd base and get into scoring position down 4-3. Then Waldschmidt got a hanging slider and did not miss it! What an electric moment and perhaps the biggest swing of the season thus far considering that the Dbacks were able to gain a game on both the Padres and the Phillies tonight on 1 single swing. What a great moment for this team!

The Dbacks will look to win the series tomorrow night and in the postgame interview Torey Lovullo insisted that Jordan Lawlar will be in the lineup tomorrow which is tremendous news for this team and for a guy that has had such unfortunate injury luck in his early career. So all is right in the desert tonight and what a tremendous boost for this team as the Dbacks will go into tomorrow 1 game out of a wild card spot!

The Diamondbacks defeated the Cubs 5-4. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images

articles.title: 'Dukh hota hai': CWG gold medallist judoka Harsh Singh rues Asian Games snub
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: âDukh hota hai. Mai iss bade chance ka wait kar rha tha par naam nahi aya [It hurts. I was waiting for this big opportunity, but my name di.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: âDukh hota hai. Mai iss bade chance ka wait kar rha tha par naam nahi aya [It hurts. I was waiting for this big opportunity, but my name didnât come up],â a dejected Harsh Singh told Timesofindia.com after being left out of the Indian judo squad for the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya.Just a month ago, Harsh made history as the first-ever male Indian judoka to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow in the menâs 60kg category.Although he did not meet the Asian Games selection criteria, he hoped his gold medal-winning performance would earn him a place in the squad. The 23-year-old believed his form and confidence after the Glasgow triumph could have helped him win another medal for India.India is going to send only three female judokas to the Asian Games - Asmita Dey, Women -48kg, Yamini Mourya - Women -57kg and Inunganbi Takhellambam - Women -70kg.What is the selection criteria?While top six in Asia via rankings was the operative standard set by SAI, in cases where judging by that marker was not possible or realistic, âa top-six finish among Asian nations in international competitionsâ, or a top-six finish at an Asian Championship would be the operative criterion.The ministry, in its release, however, added a relaxation clause: one that allowed it to choose an athlete for justifiable reasons, as recommended by experts from the concerned federation.Harsh did not meet either of the criteria, but his gold medal gave him hope of representing India at the mega event in Aichi-Nagoya.âI was told by the federation that my name was given and a total of 13 judokas names were given for Asian Games selection. I know that I didn't meet the criteria. But I was among the athletes who won the medals. I am in good touch, in form, in confidence, and I had the belief that I could win another medal for my country. But that's the life of an athlete I think,â Harsh said.Tough draw ended Asian Games hopesHarsh had a good opportunity to win an Asian Games berth when he participated in the Asian Championships, held in Ordos City, China, in April this year.As per the rules, judokas who won gold, silver or bronze medals, as well as those who fought in bronze-medal matches regardless of whether they won or lost, would qualify for the Asian Games.Unfortunately, Harsh got a tough draw and had to face Tokyo Olympics silver medallist Yang Yung-wei of Chinese Taipei. Harsh lost to Yang Yung-wei in the first round.Now, Harsh wants to leave this dejection behind and focus on the Lausanne Grand Slam.âWhen my name didnât appear on the list, I approached the federation. They said it was no longer in their hands and that nothing could be done now. I canât go to the Asian Games now, can I? So now Iâm focusing on the Lausanne Grand Slam,â he said.The electrician's son and his struggleFor years, Harsh had seen his father work as an electrician, going from home to home to repair switches, plugs, and electrical appliances in and around South West Delhiâs Dwarka locality. Whatever he earned was the livelihood of the family.The family also went through a difficult period and sometimes even struggled to arrange meals during the COVID-19 lockdown. With no one allowed to move around freely, work dried up. His father could no longer go from house to house. The daily earnings stopped completely. Sometimes it was Rs 500 to Rs 1000.The family's savings were exhausted. But despite all these tensions and worries, Harsh kept going.âAt that time, whatever little savings my father had, thatâs what we used to run the household on. That also ran out. We would borrow some money and somehow manage. But I never stopped my practice. I had decided that I had to do something for my family,â Harsh recalled.âIt was a very difficult time. Whatever savings we had were gone within two years because there were expenses for me as well. Sometimes I had to travel for competitions, and I had to maintain my diet. Even when there was no competition, we still had to maintain the same diet. So, basically, all our savings were exhausted,â he said.The turnaroundBut Harsh and his family didn't know that the struggles of his family would soon be over. The fortunes started changing within three years when Harsh won gold at the Nationals in 2024.The gold medal at the Nationals earned him a job in ITBP. After spending around eight to nine months there, Harsh received an offer from the Indian Army. He left ITBP and joined the Army as a Havaldar.âThe Indian Army has helped me a lot. Our Commandant and all the coaches, Roop Chand sir and Chandan sir, have supported me a lot. They told me, âYou focus on judo, we will take care of the rest.â The Army has said that I donât have to worry about doing a regular job while training. They have also helped by providing all the facilities and requirements, including my diet and supplements,â Harsh said.The life-changing CWG goldGlasgow brought the biggest moment of his career. For him, the CWG gold not only earned him a promotion in the Indian Army but also brought respect to his family.âThis is my first medal at the Commonwealth Games, and it is also my first international medal. This medal means a lot to me. This success is a very big thing for my family. I canât thank God enough. This medal is for my father and mother,â Harsh said.âNow, even the neighbours who didnât used to speak to us come to our house, meet my mother and father and have tea. For me, the most important thing is the respect my family has received,â he said.âI have told my father, âNow you rest and enjoy your life.â He has done a lot for me. I have seen him worried many times, but he never gave up. It is my turn now to do something for him and give him a relaxed life,â Harsh signed off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonny Lomax: St Helens legend to retire at end of 2026 Super League season
articles.summary: Jonny Lomax has made 388 appearances for St Helens, winning five Grand Finals, one Challenge Cup and a World Club Challenge; he earned four caps for Great Britain and 11 for England, which included a World Cup final appearance against Australia in 2017
articles.body:
Lomax, who has not featured since fracturing his jaw in Saints' defeat by Warrington Wolves in June, has made 388 appearances for the club, winning five Grand Finals, one Challenge Cup and a World Club Challenge.

He won four caps for Great Britain and 11 for England, which included a World Cup final appearance against Australia in 2017.

Lomax confirmed the move with a post on his Instagram that read: "At the end of 2026, I will call time on my playing career. This was something I always planned, and those closest to me have always been aware of.

"Over the last 20 years [18 professionally], I have been able to live out a boyhood dream. Achieving far more than I could ever have imagined. Representing and captaining my hometown club and, of course, the pinnacle, representing England and Great Britain.

"I will retire at the age of 36, grateful for the life the game has given me, knowing I have given it everything I could, with the scars to prove it [19 operations, including 12 knee ops by the age of 26]. Despite this, I still feel lucky.

"For those that have supported me throughout it all... I hope I have been able to do you proud."

Saints are currently on 28 points and seventh in the Super League standings, one place outside of the play-off positions with three games to go.

They need to leapfrog one of Hull KR (sixth, 30 points), Leigh Leopards (fifth, 32 points) or Wakefield Trinity (fourth, 32 points) down the stretch.

Current Super League leaders Leeds Rhinos, as well as Wigan Warriors - tied on 38 points but with an inferior point differential - and Warrington Wolves, two back in third, have already qualified for the play-offs.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: How Stephen Curry played a huge role in Golden State Warriors’ first new signing of the offseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors spent over two months of the 2026 offseason without signing a single new player to their roster before finally making an addition o...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors spent over two months of the 2026 offseason without signing a single new player to their roster before finally making an addition on August 25.

The Warriors spent most of their offseason recruiting LeBron James , a pursuit that failed. The team has been quiet since then, but made two late-August signings to bolster their roster before the season.

Guard Brandon Williams and forward Georges Niang both signed on minimum contracts with the franchise, with Stephen Curry specifically playing a crucial role in one of them joining the Warriors.

Stephen Curry recruited new signing Brandon Williams on a Zoom call

The SF Chronicle spoke to Toby Spino, Williams' coach and advisor, and revealed that Curry pitched Brandon on joining the Warriors a few months ago.

"Golden State has had a target on Williams for months. Earlier this summer… Stephen Curry set up a call with Williams to talk shop. 'When he first came in, he was like, 'Oh, I gotta go home. I got a Zoom call with Wardell.'"

Despite the call being months ago, Williams was left in a state of limbo as the Warriors were in the middle of their LeBron pursuit at the time.

Now, after a summer of primarily bringing back the roster that missed the playoffs last season, Williams became the Warriors' first addition of the summer, beating Georges Niang to that honor by a few hours.

Williams will be a backup rotational guard for the Warriors behind Curry and De'Anthony Melton. While his role depends on how the season plays out, this is a high-upside signing by GSW.

Brandon Williams' 2025-26 stats before joining the Warriors

Williams averaged 13.0 points and 3.9 assists on 47.2% from the field and 23.2% from three for the Mavericks last season.

He is a true NBA developmental story, going undrafted but staying on a two-way contract with the Mavericks for multiple seasons before finally getting a breakout opportunity last season.

His poor three-point shooting held the Mavericks back from extending him and warded off other teams looking for low-usage rotational players to stretch the floor.

The Warriors have enough floor-spacing and need genuine driving threats from the perimeter who can collapse defenses while also having the scoring touch to create their own opportunities.

Williams is also an above-average defender despite being 6'2″, primarily due to his hustle and intensity. He's a great rotational fit for the Warriors and could have a breakout season if his shot has improved, given that the Warriors have opportunities for guards like him to come in and succeed.

articles.title: Joshua Zirkzee Key To Man Utd Transfers As Interest Remains
articles.summary: Joshua Zirkzee’s potential return to Italy holds the key to Manchester United’s recruitment plans as Michael Carrick targets a new striker to solve his side'...
articles.body:
Why Man United have always needed a striker this summer.

On the field, Manchester United could not have had a worse start to the season, with a 2-0 loss to newly-promoted Hull City.

In almost every regard, the Tigers outperformed the Red Devils, which will leave Michael Carrick with many tactical headaches.

Off the field, United could be braced for a very busy week with the transfer deadline on the 1st of September on the horizon.

In terms of incomings, Carlos Baleba has now completed his move from Brighton and Hove Albion . His first words as a Manchester United player can be found here .

Outgoings could be key for United if they want to bring in more players, as the futures of some senior squad and academy players are pivotal to the club.

Joshua Zirkzee has been linked with a move away all summer, with the same Serie A clubs hovering around the player but yet to make a formal offer. However, with the transfer deadline approaching, a deal may be more likely to advance.

According to Laurie Whitwell, the likes of Juventus and Como have shown clear interest in bringing the Dutchman back to Italy , where he excelled at Bologna .

He also reported that three other unnamed Premier League clubs are interested in him. One of those clubs could be Aston Villa , with the Midlands club looking for a striker and having previously been linked with the centre forward.

The departure of Zirkzee is so important because Whitwell also suggested that if the Dutchman did leave, the club could return to the market for a striker to deputise for or compete with Benjamin Sesko .

Lisandro Martinez's Suddenly 'Fighting' To Save Career Amid Man Utd Hierarchy DoubtsPersistent injury woes may force Manchester United to offload Lisandro Martinez, as club officials demand the Argentine proves his fitness before the summer transfer window shuts.

Zirkzee is undoubtedly a good footballer with a lot of talent, but the Dutchman has failed to adapt to life at Old Trafford, meaning a departure is best for all parties.

Against Hull City and at times last season, it was abundantly clear that without a real focal point up front, the team looked lost. While Matheus Cunha (who started up front against Hull), Bryan Mbeumo , and Marcus Rashford can play there, they lack the instincts and presence of an out-and-out striker.

When Sesko came on against Hull, it was clear that the impact of having a player consistently making those runs, even if the players could not find him, was hugely beneficial.

Whether it is an experienced player like Jean-Philippe Mateta or a riskier option like the youthful Nicolò Tresoldi , a striker is needed.

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz fall in US Open mixed doubles quarterfinal
articles.summary: Star pair lost to Cobolli and Bencic, who will play married partners Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils in the semifinal.
articles.body:
The return of Serena Williams to Arthur Ashe Stadium came to an abrupt end as she and Carlos Alcaraz fell 5-4(4), 4-1 to Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic in the US Open mixed doubles quarterfinal, their magic fading after an inspired early performance.

The 23-time major winner had not competed at the crown jewel of US tennis since her tearful farewell from the sport in 2022, and fans erupted in deafening cheers as their queen took the court again on Tuesday.

The 44-year-old Williams had an easy rapport with Alcaraz, who is 21 years her junior, as the partners grinned and giggled their way past Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool 5-3, 4-1 in the opening round earlier on Tuesday.

But their firepower was extinguished by the ice-cold Cobolli and Bencic, who will play married partners Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils in a semifinal on Wednesday.

“Playing Serena and Carlos on Arthur Ashe is not easy. I was tired before the match, I’m tired now,” said the Italian Cobolli.

Williams, who is not competing in the singles, showed glimpses of her old brilliance in their opening match against Routliffe and Glasspool, blasting a 120mph (193.1km/h) ace to audible gasps from the packed house a little more than two months after she announced her stunning comeback .

Alcaraz, who has not played since April due to injury, shook off the early rust to close out the set with a forehand winner before they sprinted through the second set, embracing after the win in their matching royal purple outfits.

“It’s always such an amazing place to be here,” said Williams. “I never expected to be back on this court.”

The Roland Garros runner-up Cobolli and Tokyo Olympic champion Bencic were too tough a task, however, as Williams and Alcaraz made early mistakes and Cobolli sealed the tie-break with an ace.

The Swiss-Italian pair only upped their level from there, with no unforced errors in the second set, and gave credit to their opponents after the match.

“I don’t know how I landed on this court — to play Carlos and Serena is a great honour,” said Bencic.

The mixed doubles main draw kicked off in the second year of its revamped format, which put singles stars in the spotlight in an effort to lure more fans in a standalone spot the week before the singles main draw.

The move proved a commercial success in its debut year, drawing sellout crowds and attracting many of the sport’s biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka were beaten 1-4, 4-2, 10-2 by experienced doubles players Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova in round one, with Siniakova sealing the upset in style with an ace.

Patten and Siniakova went on to lose to Monfils and Svitolina in the quarters 5-4(6), 4-5(3), 10-8 in their second match of the day.

“The chemistry is what put us through because we understand each other even by the look at each other’s reaction or kind of mood,” said Svitolina. “We can find the right words for each other.”

Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik will play Russian pair Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev in the other semifinal on Wednesday.

Rublev and Andreeva beat last year’s champions, Italian duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori, 1-4, 4-1, 11-9 in the opening round before ousting Casper Ruud and Diana Shnaider 4-1, 4-5(9), 10-5.

Five-time US Open champion Roger Federer returned to the Arthur Ashe Stadium to play one last match for fun against longtime rival and friend Andy Roddick.

The event, billed as “An Icon Returns to New York”, packed the stands full of fans there to watch the 45-year-old from Switzerland face Roddick in a prime-time exhibition. Many wore hats with the distinctive “RF” logo that became commonplace in the sport during Federer’s decade and a half of dominance, featuring 20 Grand Slam titles.

“It’s great to be back in New York,” Federer said. “I have incredible memories, obviously, of this court, of the fans here, of the city.”

Federer reminisced about visiting for the first time to play juniors in 1998 and reaching the final. Three years later, his debut on centre court was a straight-sets loss to Andre Agassi.

Federer, who last competed at the US Open in 2019 and retired in 2022, then teamed up with John McEnroe and faced Roddick and Agassi in a doubles exhibition.
