articles.title: Saffron Cresswell on life-changing accident and new career in para-canoe
articles.summary: Saffron Cresswell was a promising eventer before a fall left her paralysed. Just eight months after first sitting in a canoe, she is heading to the Worlds.
articles.body:
After four months in hospital, Saffron Cresswell was dreading coming home.

Before she had the fall that would leave her paralysed at the age of 23, she had 25 horses that she trained and rode in a business she had been running since she was 15 and was a talented eventer on a pathway towards the Olympics.

Eight years earlier her parents had sold their house to buy a yard to support her career, with the family living in two tiny touring caravans for six years before they converted part of a barn into a home.

For years, Cresswell had been up at 5am, riding four ponies before school, then more afterwards - if she even went in. She puts her school attendance at "68% or something ridiculous" because she was "so busy riding".

'Busy' in fact turns out to be a common theme with Cresswell. During rehab at the hospital, she'd be waiting outside the gym for it to open so she could get an hour in before her physio session was even due to start.

There had only been five days during the four months where she hadn't had a visitor and so when she finally returned home to Worcestershire, where the horses had all been sold, reality was anything but hectic.

"I came home and fundamentally the next day, both my parents went out the door and went to work," says the now 25-year-old Cresswell. "So, I was home alone in a house that I couldn't really get out of and I couldn't really do anything."

There was only one thing for it: find a new sport. Little did she know that within eight months of sitting in a canoe for the first time, she would be heading for a World Championships.

Cresswell started riding when she was three, introduced to the sport by her mum, who was "horsey" but "doing low-level amateur stuff".

"I was the only child at primary school that was allowed a phone because I used to cycle from my primary school to the yard so I could start riding before my mum came home from work," she says.

She got into eventing "properly" at 13 when she produced her own young pony from beginners level to eventually representing Great Britain at three European championships.

She glances at the medals on her wall, saying: "One gold and two team silvers... so that sort of sparked the whole eventing career."

Then came the leap of faith from her parents - "much to my poor brother's trauma who was not horsey in any way" and was suddenly now sharing a caravan with his older sister - and Cresswell began running the business of riding and competing horses for other people and coaching.

Since her accident, she has not been back on a horse. Nor does she intend to.

"Because I'd done it so seriously and to such a high level that every day was about perfecting my technique and being better, I think, to get back on and not be able to do that physically, but also not even feel the horse underneath me, I think it would just be very disheartening for me," she says.

Instead, she coaches, which she says has helped her with what has turned out - surprisingly to her - the thing she would miss the most about pre-accident life.

"[What I miss] is literally just having the horse on the yard, to just go and like say 'hello' to them over the stable," she says. "And that comes from somebody who was so busy that I didn't really have loads of time to do that anyway."

The coaching is one of the new parts of the family business, which has had to change since her accident.

"The business is basically having to diversify, which is still very much an ongoing process," she says.

"My parents had given up so much to build something that allowed me to do the sport. It wasn't like we were at home and I left home and did this - they were very invested as well. So it's kind of affected everybody from that side of things."

Cresswell had been beginning to make her mark at senior level when she was competing at Bramham Horse Trials on 8 June, 2024.

Three fences before the end of her under-25 cross-country round, she came off her horse Vivendi Hero.

"I remember all of it because I didn't even get knocked out," she says. "[It was] just a freak accident.

"I just landed on the back of my head and unfortunately broke my back at T4 level - so chest level - and basically as soon as I fell, instantly knew I couldn't feel my legs."

She remembers an "awful" 45-minute ambulance ride to Leeds General Infirmary, where she had emergency surgery.

At that point, she wondered whether the damage would be permanent, because only couple of weeks previously she had been chatting to a friend - Olympic silver medallist Nicola Wilson - who had broken her neck in a fall.

"She said, 'when I fell, I couldn't feel my arm for 20 minutes, and then my feeling came back'. So when I had my accident, I had this really weird thing, like I just thought, 'oh, it's fine, it'll be 20 minutes, and my feeling will come back'," she says.

Wilson, who visited Cresswell in intensive care, regained her feeling in her legs in three or four weeks.

"So I have this really weird thing because then I was sort of waiting for three to four weeks as if I was going to get feeling back," says Cresswell, who was moved to a spinal unit in Wakefield.

"It was probably not until about six weeks that the realisation really hits... that actually this wasn't going to be the outcome that I had hoped for."

Cresswell was bedbound for six weeks in what she calls her "hotel room", a private room in the hospital where the wall was covered in get-well-soon cards.

Even then, she kept busy as the physios would give her some weights she could use for her arms.

"They were tiny, but in my head, it was a principle of having something to do every day," she says.

One of the first parts of rehab was learning to sit up again.

"With a spinal injury your blood pressure gets really lowered. So I couldn't sit up in a wheelchair for longer than about five minutes without feeling faint," says Cresswell.

Then there were things like putting on socks or tying up her hair, although even by the time she left hospital she still could not do the latter while sitting up because she did not have any core strength or balance.

She remembers her timetable at the unit - official physio was 2pm til 3pm but she would be at the gym when it opened at 1pm, having also been at the physio room at 10am when that opened.

She was determined to keep busy - and creative about how to make that happen.

Take, for example, when she was told that it would take too many people to help her swim.

"Instead of saying anything, I just used to say OK, that's fine, but can I come and sit and watch? So, I was basically just making myself known by the swimming pool," says Cresswell, who credits her athlete's mindset for her drive and ability to take positives from every situation.

"So, I went for two weeks. I sat and watched these other people in the physios do swimming.

"And funnily enough, by the third week, they thought, 'we're going to have to let her go in the swimming pool now because she's just going to annoy us otherwise'."

It turned out, water was going to become a huge part of her life.

"It was a great stepping stone to coming home. And I think I kind of held on to that when I came home initially because the first while was really tough at home."

She left hospital on 8 October and by December had started wheelchair racing, going on to race 10Ks and a half-marathon, also doing wheelchair tennis and basketball.

"I was worried I would never find a sport that I wanted to put my whole energy into," she says. "I think I knew that horses were my hobby that got to turn into my sport and my career and lifestyle so I didn't know if that would be possible to find something like that."

Cresswell had got chatting to Olympic canoe athlete Deborah Kerr at an event run by the Women's Sport Trust charity who had told her to "have a go".

So, on 23 December last year, she did. Winter was "not the time to start a water sport" and she was "not a natural".

"My coach was too scared to let me off the bank in case I capsized," she laughs. "And that probably stayed, I don't think I left the bank for about a month."

A one-off taster session turned into twice a week and then eventually five times a week on the water. Four-hour training sessions, plus gym work three days a week.

One of the biggest challenges has been staying upright.

"I don't have any feedback of any part of my body if I am losing balance," she explains. "So I'm strapped into a seat because I've got no core function, but I can't actually feel that seat. So I basically feel like I'm floating.

"So my only thing I've got to know if I've lost balance is my head and my eyes. So that took a while to start to hone in and they always say, deaf people hear better than anybody else, don't they? And I think it's a bit the same.

"It's like, I've now tuned into how to balance myself without the use of the rest of my body. But I'd say the balance aspect is a big part of it alongside the technical, constant skill-based stuff that needs to be improved."

It is the technical aspect that she thinks has similarities to equestrian and which is why she thinks she enjoys it so much.

Her progress has been rapid, by anyone's standards. Not least her own.

"World Championships was definitely not the plan. It was a quiet goal after a while that if I could get the time, I might be able to go," says Cresswell, who alongside training is also doing media work.

"The time I needed to achieve was, I think, one minute 26 seconds. And anyway, I'm now down to one minute 18. So I've kind of over-achieved on that one, which has just been through repetition, practise, finding new ways to do things."

She has been selected to represent Great Britain at this month's Canoe Sprint and Para-Canoe World Championships in Poznan, Poland.

Having only ever raced once before in the UK her aims are modest.

"Honestly, stay up and get through the start and finish line," she says, explaining that she capsized before the start of a race she was due to do in April.

It is more about getting an international classification - which involves a series of medical tests to assess an athlete's impairment and demonstrating how much of your body you can use when paddling - so that she can be eligible to earn points at events that can lead to qualification for the 2028 Paralympics in Los Angeles.

Could she have pictured this when she was in hospital?

"I certainly wouldn't have imagined I was going to do para-canoe - I didn't even know [that] was a sport when I was in hospital," says Cresswell, who will compete in the VL1 (a canoe with a support float) and KL1 (kayak).

"But to be honest, I think what actually is more kind of crazy in my head is I couldn't even imagine January me doing this."

articles.body:
After four months in hospital, Saffron Cresswell was dreading coming home.

Before she had the fall that would leave her paralysed at the age of 23, she had 25 horses that she trained and rode in a business she had been running since she was 15 and was a talented eventer on a pathway towards the Olympics.

Eight years earlier her parents had sold their house to buy a yard to support her career, with the family living in two tiny touring caravans for six years before they converted part of a barn into a home.

For years, Cresswell had been up at 5am, riding four ponies before school, then more afterwards - if she even went in. She puts her school attendance at "68% or something ridiculous" because she was "so busy riding".

'Busy' in fact turns out to be a common theme with Cresswell. During rehab at the hospital, she'd be waiting outside the gym for it to open so she could get an hour in before her physio session was even due to start.

There had only been five days during the four months where she hadn't had a visitor and so when she finally returned home to Worcestershire, where the horses had all been sold, reality was anything but hectic.

"I came home and fundamentally the next day, both my parents went out the door and went to work," says the now 25-year-old Cresswell. "So, I was home alone in a house that I couldn't really get out of and I couldn't really do anything."

There was only one thing for it: find a new sport. Little did she know that within eight months of sitting in a canoe for the first time, she would be heading for a World Championships.

Cresswell started riding when she was three, introduced to the sport by her mum, who was "horsey" but "doing low-level amateur stuff".

"I was the only child at primary school that was allowed a phone because I used to cycle from my primary school to the yard so I could start riding before my mum came home from work," she says.

She got into eventing "properly" at 13 when she produced her own young pony from beginners level to eventually representing Great Britain at three European championships.

She glances at the medals on her wall, saying: "One gold and two team silvers... so that sort of sparked the whole eventing career."

Then came the leap of faith from her parents - "much to my poor brother's trauma who was not horsey in any way" and was suddenly now sharing a caravan with his older sister - and Cresswell began running the business of riding and competing horses for other people and coaching.

Since her accident, she has not been back on a horse. Nor does she intend to.

"Because I'd done it so seriously and to such a high level that every day was about perfecting my technique and being better, I think, to get back on and not be able to do that physically, but also not even feel the horse underneath me, I think it would just be very disheartening for me," she says.

Instead, she coaches, which she says has helped her with what has turned out - surprisingly to her - the thing she would miss the most about pre-accident life.

"[What I miss] is literally just having the horse on the yard, to just go and like say 'hello' to them over the stable," she says. "And that comes from somebody who was so busy that I didn't really have loads of time to do that anyway."

The coaching is one of the new parts of the family business, which has had to change since her accident.

"The business is basically having to diversify, which is still very much an ongoing process," she says.

"My parents had given up so much to build something that allowed me to do the sport. It wasn't like we were at home and I left home and did this - they were very invested as well. So it's kind of affected everybody from that side of things."

Cresswell had been beginning to make her mark at senior level when she was competing at Bramham Horse Trials on 8 June, 2024.

Three fences before the end of her under-25 cross-country round, she came off her horse Vivendi Hero.

"I just landed on the back of my head and unfortunately broke my back at T4 level - so chest level - and basically as soon as I fell, instantly knew I couldn't feel my legs."

She remembers an "awful" 45-minute ambulance ride to Leeds General Infirmary, where she had emergency surgery.

At that point, she wondered whether the damage would be permanent, because only couple of weeks previously she had been chatting to a friend - Olympic silver medallist Nicola Wilson - who had broken her neck in a fall.

"She said, 'when I fell, I couldn't feel my arm for 20 minutes, and then my feeling came back'. So when I had my accident, I had this really weird thing, like I just thought, 'oh, it's fine, it'll be 20 minutes, and my feeling will come back'," she says.

Wilson, who visited Cresswell in intensive care, regained her feeling in her legs in three or four weeks.

"So I have this really weird thing because then I was sort of waiting for three to four weeks as if I was going to get feeling back," says Cresswell, who was moved to a spinal unit in Wakefield.

"It was probably not until about six weeks that the realisation really hits... that actually this wasn't going to be the outcome that I had hoped for."

Cresswell was bedbound for six weeks in what she calls her "hotel room", a private room in the hospital where the wall was covered in get-well-soon cards.

Even then, she kept busy as the physios would give her some weights she could use for her arms.

"They were tiny, but in my head, it was a principle of having something to do every day," she says.

One of the first parts of rehab was learning to sit up again.

"With a spinal injury your blood pressure gets really lowered. So I couldn't sit up in a wheelchair for longer than about five minutes without feeling faint," says Cresswell.

Then there were things like putting on socks or tying up her hair, although even by the time she left hospital she still could not do the latter while sitting up because she did not have any core strength or balance.

She was determined to keep busy - and creative about how to make that happen.

"Instead of saying anything, I just used to say OK, that's fine, but can I come and sit and watch? So, I was basically just making myself known by the swimming pool," says Cresswell, who credits her athlete's mindset for her drive and ability to take positives from every situation.

articles.title: Duke Champion Kyle Singler Calls Out Coach K in Alarming Videos
articles.summary: Former Duke star Kyle Singler named Coach K directly in three concerning videos, accusing his former coach of setting him up while pleading for help. The pos...
articles.body:
Former Duke star Kyle Singler directly accused Mike Krzyzewski of mistreating him and repeatedly pleaded with his former coach for help across three concerning new social media videos.

"Coach K has set me up," Singler says in one of the videos. "Set me up, man."

Singler, the Most Outstanding Player of Duke's 2010 national championship run under Krzyzewski, makes a series of serious and sometimes difficult-to-follow allegations throughout the clips. He claims people have broken into his home, taken money and compromised his accounts, while repeatedly saying he feels unable to leave his residence.

The videos provide no evidence establishing those allegations as fact.

What they do make clear is whom Singler wants to hear his message.

"Coach, where you at?" Singler says. "Help my brother out. Thought we on the same team, man."

Singler's first video is centered largely on Krzyzewski, who coached him for all four of his seasons at Duke.

"I have no power. I have no house," Singler says. "I've reached out to coach and everybody has turned the other way."

Singler then alleges that his power has been cut off and that people have broken into his house, stolen money and ruined his life.

"Reached out to Coach K," Singler says. "And all he did is sit me on the bench."

It isn't clear what Singler means by being put on the bench. Krzyzewski retired from coaching Duke following the 2021-22 season, more than a decade after Singler's college career ended.

Neither Krzyzewski nor Duke appears to have publicly responded to Singler's latest statements.

Singler Also Makes Accusation Involving Duke

The second video contains another direct appeal to his former coach and expands Singler's claims to Duke.

Singler says he has experienced confrontations while living in Oklahoma and claims he feels unable to leave his home.

"Coach, I need your help," he says. "Help, man. I'm stuck at my house and I can't leave. I feel imprisoned."

Singler later says his "life's on the line" and alleges that people are breaking into his home and accounts and taking money.

"Duke's all about it," Singler says. "I got Duke again begging for my money. Everybody's after my money, trying to kill me."

Those are Singler's allegations, and the videos do not establish that Duke, Krzyzewski or anyone affiliated with the university has engaged in the conduct he describes.

Singler concludes by again speaking directly to his former coach.

"Coach, you got again former player being mistreated and abused and you ain't doing nothing, man," he says. "Help out."

Third Video Continues Singler's Plea for Help

Singler continues the theme in a third clip, saying that his accounts are "hijacked and frozen" and claiming that people are watching his residence.

He again turns to the coach he addressed throughout the other videos.

"I need your help," Singler says. "I'm locked in my house and I have no freedom anymore."

Near the end, Singler says he has attempted to contact his former coach "many times" and accuses him of being "deflective" and leaving people behind.

"So, you got a player that's been traded, baby," Singler says.

It is unclear what Singler means by that remark. His professional basketball career ended years ago.

The new posts arrive after previous videos from Singler generated widespread concern within basketball.

In November 2024, Singler posted a video saying he had been mistreated and that he feared for his life. The Associated Press reported that the National Basketball Players Association subsequently contacted his family. Kevin Love, Isaiah Thomas and Andre Drummond were among the current and former NBA players who publicly offered support.

"I love you Kyle. Hit me whenever. Please," Love wrote at the time, according to the AP.

Singler later encountered legal trouble in Oklahoma. In October 2025, he was charged with one misdemeanor count of assault and battery in the presence of a child after an alleged incident involving his girlfriend, according to the Associated Press. Singler was released on bond after his arrest, the AP reported.

The latest three videos put his relationship with Duke back at the center of the story.

Singler wasn't a peripheral player under Krzyzewski. He spent four seasons at Duke, helped deliver the 2010 national championship and was named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player.

That history makes his repeated appeals particularly striking now.

Across all three videos, amidst a collection of allegations and grievances, Singler repeatedly comes back to one request directed at the coach with whom he won college basketball's biggest prize:

articles.title: US Open mixed doubles prize money, format and teams – including Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: The second edition of the new-look mixed doubles tournament at Flushing Meadows takes place this week
articles.body:
The high-profile mixed doubles event at the US Open is underway with several star pairings in action at Flushing Meadows.

Serena Williams , who returned to tennis in June, partnered up with defending men's singles champion Carlos Alcaraz in New York – but the high-profile duo proved no match for Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals.

World No 1 women's player Aryna Sabalenka and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic were the top seeds but lost in the first round, with the all-American pairing of Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz the second seeds.

The Italian doubles pairing of Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori were the defending champions, but also made an early exit.

Here's everything you need to know for the US Open mixed doubles event.

The main draw starts on Tuesday 25 August with the first round and quarter-finals. Play starts at 4pm BST (11am local) on Arthur Ashe Stadium and 3pm BST (10am local) on Louis Armstrong Stadium.

The semi-finals and final will headline a special night session on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday 26 August, starting at midnight BST (7pm local).

Katerina Siniakova/Henry Patten bt. Aryna Sabalenka/Novak Djokovic [1] 1-4, 4-2, 2-10

Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils bt. Alexandra Eala/Felix Auger-Aliassime 4-1, 4-1

Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli [4] bt. Taylor Townsend/Alexander Zverev 4-2, 4-2

Serena Williams/Carlos Alcaraz bt. Erin Routliffe/Lloyd Glasspool 5-3, 4-1

Karolina Muchova/Jakub Mensik bt. Kristina Mladenovic/Marcelo Arevalo 4-1, 2-4, 10-7

Emma Navarro/Tommy Paul bt. Amanda Anisimova/Learner Tien [3] 5-3, 4-2

Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev bt. Sara Errani/Andrea Vavassori 1-4, 4-1, 11-9

Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud bt. Jessica Pegula/Taylor Fritz [2] 4-2, 4-1

Svitolina/Monfils bt Siniakova/Patten 5-4, 4-5, 10-8

Bencic/Cobolli [4] bt. Williams/Alcaraz 5-4, 4-1

Muchova/Mensik bt. Navarro/Paul 4-1, 5-3

Andreeva/Rublev vs Shnaider/Ruud 4-1, 4-5, 10-4

For every match up to the final, matches will be best-of-3 sets, with sets to four games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

For the final, it will be a traditional set to six games and a 10-point tie-break instead of a third set.

All matches will have sudden death deuce.

Matches in the United Kingdom will be broadcast on Sky Sports Tennis .

In the United States, ESPN2 will present live coverage, with the final on ESPN and ESPN+.

Photos of Garrettsville Garfield boys soccer vs. Crestwood

The Rovers moved to 3-0-0 behind two goals in the first 127 seconds and a couple of insurance goals in the second half. Senior Zach Pastor ripped the first goal of the game from the left side in the second minute. Exactly a minute later, junior Dylan Boland capped a beautiful run in which he halted, turned inward and then fired away for a 2-0 Rootstown lead. Crestwood hung around the rest of the half, including Owen Overfield's free-kick goal from 35 yards out in the eighth minute. The Rovers finally got the insurance they were seeking in the 54th minute when Bryson Scarlett slotted a perfect pass up to fellow senior Sam Textor for a goal. Pastor added further insurance with his second goal of the game.

Roosevelt 189, Cloverleaf 193, Tallmadge 266

The Rough Riders snapped the Colts' 118-match conference win streak behind junior Brooke Beatty's 39, including birdies on the fifth and eighth holes. Senior Aubrey Byler added a 49 while junior Makenna Ward (50) and senior Coco Golden (51) rounded out the scoring.

Freshman Layla Haynes erupted for four goals to push the Rovers' unbeaten streak to three games. Josie App, Paisley Day and Elliott Smallfield added a goal apiece for Rootstown (2-1-1, 1-0-0 CVC) while Sammy Smolk and Charlie Wilson each tallied an assist.

Brooklyn Wilson scored twice as the Falcons remained undefeated. Molly Murphy added a goal and an assist for Field (4-0-0, 2-0-0 Metro Athletic Conference) while Odessa Hottensmith and Ruby Roberts also scored goals and Peyton Schock added an assist. Zoe Kramer made three saves to record the shutout in net.

Rootstown def. United 25-23, 25-23, 23-25, 25-21

Byers also had eight assists, eight digs and two aces while Kamenash had a team-high three aces. Ella Hayn added a team-high 23 digs for Rootstown (2-0).

Bloomfield def. Windham 25-23, 23-25, 24-26, 30-28, 15-11

The Bombers lost a heartbreaker in which the first four sets were all decided by the minimum two points. Windham fell despite Makenna Jones' 13 kills, Kyleigh Simpson's 11 assists and Kierrah Sanders' 12 digs. Makenzi Blockinger added a stellar performance from the service line with 13 points (including six aces).

The Vikings fell despite two goals from Alexis Henry and two assists from Koralee Jenior. Abigail Roberts had six saves for Waterloo (1-2-0, 0-1-0 Mahoning Valley Athletic Conference), which actually led in both corner kicks (4-2) and shots on goal (15-10).

The Rovers (1-5) fell despite Charlie Wilson firing a 50 and Morgan Giebel tacking on a solid 52.

articles.title: ‘We Weren’t Super Emotional’ – Jessica Pegula Details How Her Billionaire Parents Influenced Her Personality
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her par...
articles.body:
Jessica Pegula has an inkling as to where her impressive leadership skills may have come from, tracing them back to one of her parents in particular. Her parents, Terry and Kim Pegula, are co-owners of the NFL's Buffalo Bills and the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, with a combined net worth of $9.3 billion, according to Forbes.

What Jessica Pegula Said About Her Parents' Personalities

Pegula arrived at the US Open on the back of runner-up finishes at the Mubadala DC Open and the Cincinnati Open. Riding on that momentum, the American will be aiming to clinch her maiden Grand Slam title at the New York Major when the singles contest gets underway on Sunday, August 30.

Ahead of her campaign, Pegula sat down with Jon Wertheim for a Sports Illustrated interview in which she offered insight into her personality.

After being praised for her leadership skills, the 32-year-old attributed the quality to her directness and communication abilities, traits she believes she inherited from her mother, Kim, who has been incapacitated since suffering a cardiac arrest in 2022.

"Well, that's a nice compliment. I'm very direct, and I think I'm very honest. But I also think I communicate it pretty well, where it's not taken the wrong way. But I'm definitely pretty direct, and I think I don't know if I got that from my mom," Pegula said .

"I want to say I think she was the same way: very direct with what she thought, and I think [she] was pretty thoughtful in the way she always put things, whether it was to employees or to us or stuff around work. So I think I probably got it from my mom," she added.

The world No. 3 revealed that she and her mother had a different temperament from her father Terry's more emotional personality, saying, "We weren't super emotional. I would say my dad's probably a little bit more emotional. I think my mom and I were definitely more the same personality, like kind of laid back."

In contrast to her laid-back demeanor, Pegula shared that her mind typically races during matches and that she often talks to herself on the court.

"I'm very laid back, but at the same time, I'm thinking a lot out on the court, and so I think maybe some people think I just kind of just go with whatever's happening on the court. But I'm actually thinking quite a bit—like a lot. I talk to myself a lot. I'm constantly running," she said.

The world No. 3 disclosed that the same trait carried over when she played other sports recreationally, much to the exasperation of her husband, Taylor Gahagen, during golf sessions.

"I think when I'm competing—even when I play other sports for fun—I love to just talk to myself and talk myself through things a lot of the time out loud," she added. "And that's where, like my husband, if we're playing golf, he's just like, Just hit the ball. I need to talk through things, so maybe it's a little contradictory with my laid-backness."

articles.title: LeBron James’ LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter-led Guggenheim before joining LA Lakers
articles.summary: Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers, Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company. In 2018, as Jam...
articles.body:
Prior to either of their associations with the LA Lakers , Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners lent LeBron James $300 million for a new company.

In 2018, as James geared up to sign with the Lakers in free agency, part of his decision to move to the City of Angels was because of his desire to pursue outside business ventures.

Part of this involved setting up a new LLC, which required a massive injection of cash flow. Unbeknownst to him at the time, the man who would end up buying the Lakers seven years later played a crucial part in this.

LeBron James' LLC borrowed $300 million from Mark Walter's Guggenheim Partners

According to reporting from Bloomberg , just a few months prior to him signing with the Los Angeles Lakers, LeBron James got into business with future team owner Mark Walter.

In 2018, James' LLC borrowed $300 million from two life insurance companies that were associated with Guggenheim Partners.

At the time, Walter was the CEO of Guggenheim Partners. The amount is due in 2049, allowing James the cash flow his company needed, being leveraged against James' sponsorship and non-NBA earnings.

Furthermore, in 2022, James signed a $97 million contract extension with the Lakers. At the same time, his LLC borrowed more cash from the pair of insurance companies against bonds worth $60 million with an interest rate of 5.75%.

These transactions were approved by the NBA at the time, as they explained in a statement to Fox Business when asked about the matter.

"The 2018 and 2022 transactions were a securitisation done by Mr. James with his personal, non-NBA salary, assets and income, which is a very common financial structure for an individual with this level of earnings and assets.

"Both transactions were fully approved by NBA. Mr. James has no affiliation with Guggenheim, Sammons Financial, North American Life or Midland National beyond their participation in these transactions."

Fast forward to the summer of 2025, and James would become a direct associate of Walter, who purchased the LA Lakers for a then-record $10 billion.

Since James' departure this summer, Walter has sold the Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner for a whopping $12.5 billion, amid an investigation into his financial activity.

Roma had inquired about signing Ziolkowski for around €7-8 million, in addition to two foreign clubs who had made official offers to Roma. However, at this price, Roma are now prioritizing a loan move.

articles.title: How will Barcelona line up against Athletic?
articles.summary: Hansi Flick’s possible XI for Thursday’s clash
articles.body:
Barcelona look for a strong start to their La Liga home campaign as the reigning back-to-back champions face historic rivals Athletic Club at Camp Nou.

Here's how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Thursday's battle:

Barça got off to an excellent start at the weekend against Elche and now return home where they finished last season with a historic perfect record at Camp Nou, and Flick will be looking to ride the momentum of the team that played so well in the second half on Sunday.

We will likely see only one change at the back since Andreas Christensen needs to be managed carefully and isn't expected to start two games in four days, so Pau Cubarsí will probably make his season debut after his summer glory with Spain.

Gerard Martín is Cubarsí's trusted partner and will start again at center-back, with Eric Garcia picked ahead of Jules Kounde at right-back and young Xavi Espart retaining his place on the left given the fact João Cancelo is still not fully fit and Alejandro Balde 's status is uncertain at best.

Even though Gavi survived an injury scare at the weekend and only suffered a bruise on his knee, it's prudent not to risk him in this one so Pedri will take his place in the lineup alongside Marc Bernal and Fermín López .

We are all excited to see the debut of new signing Rodri that could very well happen in this one, but he's had just a couple of sessions with the squad and will likely come off the bench to get a great ovation from the home crowd in the second half.

Barça's attack put on a show in the second half on Sunday and the noise about the striker position has quieted down for now, especially after Raphinha 's amazing performance as a center-forward. He will start in that spot again, with Karim Adeyemi keeping his place on the left after an excellent competitive debut at the weekend.

Lamine Yamal is very much in preseason form and needs minutes to gain rhythm, so the teenager will start again on the right looking to bounce back from a supbar display against Elche.

Possible XI : Joan; Eric, Cubarsí, Martín, Espart; Fermín, Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Raphinha, Adeyemi (4-3-3)

articles.title: Report: Ipswich Town set to land €27.5m World Cup winner
articles.summary: Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels SignificantIpswich Town’s summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and th...
articles.body:
Exequiel Palacios to Ipswich? Why This Argentina Midfielder Link Feels Significant

Ipswich Town's summer rebuild in midfield already has a clear shape, and the latest report adds another intriguing layer. According to The Athletic , Ipswich have already moved decisively, with "Ipswich have signed midfielders Sasa Lukic from Fulham and Florentino Luis from Burnley this summer, after Jens Cajuste and Dan Neil departed the club following the conclusion of their loan spells."

That alone tells the story of a club refusing to stand still. Ipswich are refreshing the engine room with experience, physicality and pedigree, and Exequiel Palacios would elevate that strategy again. The 27-year-old arrives in this conversation with serious credentials. As outlined in the report, "Palacios, 27, joined Leverkusen from River Plate in 2020." In that time, "He has made 185 appearances for the club, providing 15 goals and 17 assists, and was part of the side that won the Bundesliga title in 2023-24."

For Ipswich, that sort of background matters. This is not a developmental gamble in the usual sense, it is a player who has operated in title-winning environments and handled the demands of top-level football in Germany and on the international stage. There is, of course, context around his recent availability. "He featured 25 times in all competitions last season either side of four months out with a right adductor injury." That will naturally be part of any assessment, especially for a side looking to add reliability as well as quality.

Still, the ceiling is obvious. "Palacios has been capped 41 times at international level by Argentina." More than that, "He was part of the side that won the 2022 World Cup and was included in the squad for the 2026 tournament but featured just once in the tournament in their final group game against Jordan ." Even limited recent tournament minutes do not diminish the stature he would bring to Portman Road.

From an Ipswich perspective, this would signal intent. Lukic and Florentino Luis suggest structure and control, while Palacios would add craft, composure and proven quality in possession. For a club trying to establish itself and push forward under Gary O'Neil, signing a midfielder with Bundesliga and Argentina pedigree would represent a notable statement.

The attraction here is not only reputation, it is fit. Ipswich needed to respond after losing Cajuste and Neil, and they appear to be targeting players who can immediately raise the standard. If this move progresses, it could become one of the most eye-catching deals of their summer.

As an Ipswich supporter, this is exactly the kind of report that gets you excited. We all knew the midfield needed fresh energy after the loan departures, but bringing in players with this calibre would feel like a major step forward. Lukic and Florentino Luis already suggest the club are thinking bigger, smarter and with real purpose. If Palacios joins that mix, suddenly this midfield has depth, authority and proper top-level know-how.

What stands out most is the mentality he would bring. Anyone who has been around a Bundesliga title-winning squad and an Argentina set-up packed with elite players understands pressure, expectation and quality. That can rub off on everyone around him. At a club like Ipswich, where momentum and belief mean so much, that matters enormously.

There will be some concern over the injury record, and that is fair. Missing four months is not a minor issue. But this is where trust in the recruitment team comes in. If Ipswich believe he is ready and the medical side checks out, then it is easy to see why supporters would back the move.

Most of all, this report feels like confirmation that Ipswich are not here to make up the numbers. These are not timid moves. These are ambitious midfield targets, and fans should embrace that. If the club can land someone of Palacios' profile, Portman Road will believe anything is possible this season.

articles.title: Red Bull Gets Second Chance at Power Unit Upgrade
articles.summary: Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.
articles.body:
Red Bull has the fate of its engine hanging in the balance, at least when it comes to making improvements this season.

During the last Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) check at the start of the season, Red Bull was found to have the strongest power unit.

There was a full-on bench test, where Red Bull was deemed more than 2% ahead of every other manufacturer, meaning no extra development time, spending, or ability to introduce a new power unit upgrade.

ZANDVOORT, NETHERLANDS – AUGUST 22: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains on track during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Netherlands at Circuit Zandvoort on August 22, 2026 in Zandvoort, Netherlands. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) // Getty Images

Red Bull fought the assessment directly with the FIA, but in the end, FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis and the regulatory body found it a valid conclusion.

"Our measurement, in my opinion, has proven to be very accurate," he said.

"With that said, has everything worked fine? No, because obviously people are not happy and so on. So do we need to think about improvements in the future? Yes, I would say so."

Now, before the Italian Grand Prix, there will be a second ADUO review that could give Red Bull a second chance to get extra development support.

At this point, Red Bull is at best the third-fastest car at most tracks, but usually the fourth- or third-fastest.

An engine upgrade could be what takes their car into race-winning contention.

Max Verstappen | Photo Credit: Red Bull Content Pool

However, Tombazis is not convinced these upgrades are worthwhile or impactful in the grand scheme of things.

"I don't think it would be convenient for you to always be below, just to sort of keep getting more opportunities," he said. "What's the point of opportunities if it isn't ultimately for you to be on top?

"I think the system is working as it was designed. I do think there are some weaknesses that we need to address in the future, for sure, to make it less time-consuming, less controversial. We do need to make some steps to improve it in the future."

Red Bull, while doing a ton of aerodynamic work, begs to differ and will fight for a power unit development opportunity and a chance to challenge the class-leading Mercedes car.

articles.title: 4 things to watch for Commanders in joint practice with Ravens
articles.summary: Here are four things to watch for Commanders in joint practice with Ravens.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders headed to Owings Mills, Md., on Tuesday for Wednesday's scheduled joint practice with the Baltimore Ravens . After Saturday's disappointing performance in a 17-13 loss to the Detroit Lions , Wednesday's practice holds more weight than the final preseason game on Friday.

While the final preseason game could determine a few final roster spots for the Commanders, the joint practice with Baltimore is a final opportunity for Washington's starters to get some work against the Ravens' starters. It matters for the Commanders because their starting offense didn't play in the first preseason game and had only three snaps in the loss at Detroit.

What does Washington need to see in Wednesday's practice? Here are four things to watch on Wednesday in Owings Mills.

By all accounts, Daniels has enjoyed an excellent training camp. He looks comfortable in David Blough 's new offense. His accuracy has matched what we saw in his 2024 rookie season. So far, so good, but the Commanders would like to see Daniels have a successful day against the Ravens. Remember, he performed well against the Dolphins in the joint practice two weeks ago, but Baltimore presents a very different challenge. With Daniels unlikely to play in Friday's preseason finale, Wednesday's practice is his final regular-season tuneup. A strong performance against the Ravens from Daniels and the first-team offense would alleviate some of the concerns that arose from Saturday's performance.

This story continues to evolve. It feels like we've been discussing this position since March. Washington still doesn't know what it has in Nick Allegretti at center because he lacks experience there. But the Commanders have repeatedly expressed confidence in the veteran. He will not participate, as he continues to recover from a calf strain that has sidelined him all camp. Washington knows what it has in Julian Good-Jones. He's not a starting-quality player. The Commanders should give rookie Matt Gulbin the entire scrimmage to work with each quarterback, especially Daniels. He needs the reps. It will be interesting to see how Gulbin performs against Baltimore's front seven. This is a big test.

With Washington's starters on the practice field on Wednesday, which receiver will line up as the No. 3 receiver behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs ? While Blough isn't going to show too much in a practice or preseason game, we'll learn a lot by seeing who gets most of the reps as the third wideout. Luke McCaffrey , Treylon Burks , Antonio Williams , Dyami Brown , Van Jefferson and Jaden Bradley will all get some run, but this could be a test to see who the Commanders trust the most as WR3.

With Will Harris gone, Washington's safety position is set. We know the five the Commanders will keep and have a good idea of their roles. At cornerback, things are less certain. We know Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson are the top two, with Trey Amos still out. Baltimore's receivers, specifically Zay Flowers , will present a unique challenge for the secondary. How will the Commanders handle Flowers' quickness and his release? Who will have the responsibility of covering Flowers? The corner position remains a concern heading into the regular season with Ahkello Witherspoon 's retirement and Amos' injury. It wouldn't be shocking to see Washington add another cornerback, but this group has another chance to impress against the Ravens.

El periodista fue especialmente duro con el Barcelona por su actuación alrededor de Julián Álvarez, pero también mostró su rechazo al 'Tiempo de revisión' y analizó el regreso de Mourinho al banquillo del Real Madrid. El futuro de Julián Álvarez fue uno de los asuntos centrales. Gómez cargó directamente contra el Barcelona por sus movimientos alrededor del futbolista. "Lo que está haciendo el Barcelona es un chantaje brutal, que pare ya", aseguró. El periodista señaló directamente a los responsables de la entidad azulgrana: "Basta ya, lo que ha sido impresentable y no tiene nombre es lo que ha hecho Laporta y lo que ha hecho Deco". Y cerró su reflexión con otra afirmación contundente: "Yo creo que lo que ha intentado el Barcelona es asaltar, literalmente, el Atlético de Madrid. Esto no se puede consentir". Antes de abordar el mercado, Roberto Gómez había mostrado su enorme enfado con el 'Tiempo de revisión'. La expulsión de Yuri fue uno de los ejemplos que utilizó para explicar su postura. "Que lo quiten. Yo soy el Athletic y ahora mismo me voy al juzgado de guardia. Y digo: 'Señores, ¿qué ha pasado aquí? ¿Pero esto qué es? Esto es una vergüenza. Que lo quiten ya". Gómez considera que el sistema puede convertirse en un problema durante toda la temporada: "Que no haya otra jornada más de revisión. Es una manipulación total". También recordó otras decisiones arbitrales que considera polémicas: "Hay dos acciones en Sevilla en el primer partido que son brutales y quedan despachadas de una manera impresentable. Lo mismo que la acción de la patada de Cala a Vinicius". El periodista terminó siendo categórico: "¿Qué les parece el sistema de revisión? Es una vergüenza. Es una vergüenza". También reclamó que los árbitros se centren en su preparación: "Que se dediquen, en lugar de revisar, que se dediquen a prepararse bien, a concienciarse bien". Otro de los grandes asuntos de la intervención fue el regreso de Mourinho al Bernabéu. Roberto Gómez elogió al portugués y explicó cómo interpreta su vuelta: "Vuelve a un hábitat en donde él ha estado muy a gusto durante los años que estuvo en el Bernabéu. Ha vuelto, indudablemente, con una tranquilidad, probablemente por los años, por la experiencia y por saber dónde vuelve". Eso sí, considera que el portugués llega con la máxima exigencia. "El Real Madrid lo ha traído para que gane", afirmó. Y fue más allá al enumerar los objetivos: "Tiene la obligación de ganar, y de ganar Champions, Liga y Copa". Roberto Gómez también respaldó públicamente la postura del entrenador con Vinicius: "Me parece muy bien la protección que quiere tener sobre Vinicius". Según el periodista, el brasileño "se ha convertido en objetivo de muchísimas defensas" y existe "muy poca protección por parte de los árbitros". Por eso concluyó: "Esta protección que le quiere dar Mourinho desde un principio me parece tremendamente correcta".

articles.title: Raúl Fuentes desvela los planes del Barça para el final de mercado: Julián Álvarez y varias salidas
articles.standfirst: El periodista explicó la situación de la plantilla azulgrana y aseguró que Casadó y Fort saldrán, mientras que el club estaría dispuesto a estudiar una buena oferta por Koundé.
articles.summary: El periodista explicó la situación de la plantilla azulgrana y aseguró que Casadó y Fort saldrán, mientras que el club estaría dispuesto a estudiar una buena oferta por Koundé.
articles.body: El Barcelona afronta los últimos días del mercado con varios frentes abiertos. Raúl Fuentes explicó en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, la hoja de ruta azulgrana para este tramo final, tanto en el capítulo de llegadas como en el de salidas. Una planificación en la que Julián Álvarez continúa siendo el gran objetivo para la delantera. Según explicó Fuentes, la postura del Barça respecto al '9' está muy definida después de la reunión que mantuvieron Laporta, Deco, Flick y Bojan: "La estrategia a seguir es, en cuanto al delantero centro, o viene Julián Álvarez o no viene nadie, como mínimo hasta el mercado invernal". El periodista señaló además los esfuerzos que estaría realizando el delantero para intentar vestir de azulgrana: "Más de lo que está haciendo Julián por querer vestir la camiseta del Barça no se puede hacer más, entonces el Barça no lo va a dejar tirado hasta que se cierre el mercado". Fuentes también apuntó a la posibilidad de un nuevo movimiento económico: "Yo creo que el Barça puede subir un poco la oferta de los 100 millones que presentó a final del mes de junio". El mercado de salidas también promete movimiento durante los próximos días. En este sentido, Fuentes fue contundente con dos futbolistas de la plantilla: "Casadó y Fort se van a ir". Pero no serían los únicos nombres a seguir. El periodista puso encima de la mesa otras dos situaciones: "Luego también hay un par de patatas calientes, la patata caliente de Alejandro Balde después de dejarle fuera de la lista el domingo en Elche, y el tema de Koundé, que es un tema diferente al de Balde". Especialmente significativo es el caso de Jules Koundé. Fuentes aseguró que el francés cuenta con mercado en la Premier y explicó su situación actual en los planes de Hansi Flick: "Es un jugador que tiene buen mercado en Inglaterra". Además, añadió: "Ahora Koundé para Flick es, digamos, el tercer central, no lo ve de lateral porque el lateral es Eric García". Una situación que podría provocar que el Barça escuchase propuestas por el francés en este tramo final del mercado: "Si llega algo interesante por Koundé, pues el club se lo miraría con buenos ojos". La portería es otro de los asuntos que tiene que resolver el Barcelona. David Bernabéu habló de la llegada de Livakovic y de la posibilidad de que finalmente permanezca esta misma temporada en el equipo: "Yo creo que será para esta". El periodista fue especialmente crítico con el estado físico de Szczesny: "Está muy mal físicamente. Tú le ves la estampa y parece un jugador o un portero de Tercera Catalana". También reconoció, sin embargo, el peso que tiene el polaco dentro del vestuario: "Para Flick en el vestuario es una pieza importante". Bernabéu aseguró haber hablado con jugadores de la plantilla sobre el papel del guardameta: "Ellos te dicen que están encantados con él, que hace mucho grupo, que les da muchos consejos". La situación podría terminar influyendo en los planes con Livakovic. Según explicó David Bernabéu, "el Barça le ha firmado cuatro años a Livakovic y la idea inicial era cederle una temporada para recuperarle al final del contrato del polaco", aunque considera que el escenario ha cambiado y que el guardameta podría quedarse ya en la plantilla azulgrana.

Christian Gonzalez has been speaking to the media about his contract talks with the New England Patriots this week.

At present, Gonzalez is on a 4-year rookie contract worth $15.1 million with the Patriots. That deal is said to run through the 2026 season with the option of an extension in 2027.

There has been much talk about the Patriots star getting a new deal, but at present, he is yet to pen fresh terms.

Christian Gonzalez frustrated over New England Patriots contract talks

Gonzalez is now back in training with the Patriots ahead of the new season getting underway following an injury problem.

Now, he has spoken about his contract situation ahead of their next pre-season match against the Cleveland Browns .

When doing so, as per the New York Post , Gonzalez initially said: "I'm not going to get into that. I'm out here now. So it is what it is."

However, he then went on to express his frustration at the situation, saying: "It's frustrating. But I'm focused on the season. I'm focused on here now and doing what I have to do. I'm out here to compete and get better."

The Patriots take on the Cleveland Browns on Thursday evening in what will be their final pre-season match.

They will then kick off their proper campaign on September 9 against the Seattle Seahawks .

articles.title: Keenan Allen changed Ashton Dulin's role. Now the Colts may use him everywhere.
articles.summary: Veteran Ashton Dulin has been the Colts' No. 2 healthy receiver in training game but may drop to No. 4, opening up roles on special teams.
articles.body:
Brian Mason has never been shy in his views of Ashton Dulin 's performance on special teams, calling the 29-year-old receiver veteran "one of the three-best special teams players in the NFL" last fall.

How much the Colts will be able to take advantage of those skills – on his most active days, Indianapolis uses his 4.4 speed as its primary gunner on punt coverage, as well as one of its two returners on kickoffs – may vary week-to-week, depending on the team's health across the board.

After last week's signing of six-time Pro Bowl receiver Keenan Allen , Dulin finds himself no longer in contention for one of the Colts ' three starting wideout spots. Instead he's jockeying with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine for fourth on the depth chart on a team whose star second-year tight end Tyler Warren makes Dulin or Westbrook-Ikhine the fifth receiving option at-best.

NFL preseason; Indianapolis Colts against Atlanta Falcons

Dulin has performed arguably the most consistently of Indianapolis' rotational wideouts in the preseason, all while taking very few reps on special teams. It gave the appearance the Colts planned to significantly reduce his role on punt and kick teams to preserve his energy and impact for offense. But with Allen's signing dropping Dulin a spot, the receiver who has just seven catches since the end of the 2022 campaign finds himself in virtually the same spot as the end of last season.

"How many phases and plays he gets on special teams will just be dictated by how many plays (the offensive coaches) anticipate him getting in a game," Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason told reporters Monday. "We usually meet at the beginning of a regular season game week, and we'll kinda project who'll be up for the week and how much they plan to play.

"If they say, 'He's going to play this number of plays' on offense, that will then determine whether he plays in one, two or three phases on special teams."

As Mason went on to explain, the Colts plan to look at Dulin as a potential punt returner this week, among a long list of kick return spots. Among players in the NFL in 2025 with more than one kickoff return attempt, Dulin's 32.3-yard average ranked third-best in the league, but in the background, Mason said Dulin has been working on his punt return skills for two years.

Through two preseason games, second-year receiver Coleman Owen has been the Colts' most consistent and active returner on kicks and punts, with rookie running back Seth McGowan and rookie receiver Deion Burks , shuffling through in preseason action. Incumbent starting returner Anthony Gould has been out for much of camp with a groin injury, while the team lost frequent returner Ameer Abdullah in free agency. Josh Downs has taken reps on punt return, but the team would like to limit that given his increasing role in the offense.

Mason went on to explain that Dulin's lack of special teams reps throughout training camp came, in part, so the team could evaluate its young fringe roster players to narrow in on final contenders for various roles he would be a finalist for, pending his responsibilities on offense.

"We planned on using Ashton Dulin in roles no matter what, whether that be on kick return or at gunner. If he ever needs a sub at gunner, we can always give him a sub, but we certainly still want to have the threat of being able to use him and our opponent knowing there's a good chance he still may be out there," Mason said. "I think that does affect certain people's punt return game plan.

"If Ashton Dulin is on the field for the punt team, you certainly have to account for him and you certainly need to probably (double-team) him in order to prevent him from causing problems."
